events.event_narrative: Four and a half inches of rainfall occurred at Manning Camp in the Rincon Mountains in less than 2 hours causing excessive runoff into area washes.
Large tree limbs were downed due to gusts from a thunderstorm.
A wind gust to 75 mph occurred at Douglas-Bisbee airport.
A trained spotter estimated wind gusts to 60 mph.
Several large trees were downed at the Tucson Omni National Resort.
A power pole was knocked down at 2nd Ave. and Thatcher St. in Safford.

A man hiking in the Pinaleno Mountains became lost on February 1. Several inches of snow fell on February 2 and coincided with wind chills around 10 degrees. Air temperatures dropped into the single digits overnight. Search teams were able to follow tracks in the snow but found the man deceased. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined that the cause of death was hypothermia.

A migrant became lost while traversing the Chiricahua Mountains February 2. Several inches of snow fell late in the day and coincided with wind chills around 10 degrees. Wind chill temperatures dropped to as low as 5 below zero overnight. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined that the cause of death for this female was hypothermia.

Arizona Dept. of Transportation weather stations measured wind gusts of 58 to 62 mph along I-10 between Willcox and the New Mexico state line. Visibilities were reduced to between a quarter and a half mile in blowing dust.

The human caused Hope Fire was spread across 25 acres of grass and brush by wind gusts over 50 mph. One house and one mobile home were destroyed by the fire in the community of Cochise near the intersection of Apache Way and Quarterhorse Lane.

Temperatures in the upper 20 to lower 30s were observed during the early morning hours of February 24, and were preceded by a quarter inch of rain that fell on the 23rd. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that hypothermia was the primary cause of death for one adult male in the desert in the Ironwood National Forest northwest of Tucson.
Strong winds blew down a 20-year old Acacia tree in Oro Valley.
KALK Pioneer Field measured a wind gust of 60 mph at 1529MST.

events.event_narrative: The human caused Border Fire started on March 19 south of Arivaca near the International Border in Santa Cruz County. The wildfire was driven by wind gusts to 40 mph at times and over 1500 acres were burned in the first 24 hours. The fire was contained March 23 after it consumed a total of 1780 acres and was completely extinguished March 31. Fire suppression costs tallied $140,000.

events.event_narrative: The human caused Presumido Peak Fire started March 26 twenty miles northwest of Sasabe in the Baboquivari Mountains in southern Pima County. The wildfire burned over 1000 acres in the first 24 hours and was driven by wind gusts near 40 mph at times. It consumed a total of 2591 acres before rain on March 29 helped forward progress to be stopped by March 31. The fire was completed extinguished by April 3. Fire suppression costs tallied over $800,000.

Hot temperatures 10 to 15 degrees above normal, near 90 degrees, were experienced in southeast Pima County on March 26 causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be approached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one male found in the desert seven miles southeast of Green Valley.
Flooding reported across Highway 191 with 2.5 inches of rainfall in one hour.

The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one male found in the desert 15 miles west of Douglas.
A trained spotter reported three quarters of an inch sized hail.

Davis Monthan Air Force Base recorded a gust to 64 mph as the result of a wet microburst. Nearby damage just east of the base included 13 power poles downed and a roof blown off a home and onto several cars in the vicinity of Escalante Road just to the east of Kolb Road.

Heavy rainfall on the Mexican side of the border caused flash flooding in the city of Nogales, Arizona. This was caused by a damaged portion of the underground Nogales Wash. Local emergency management reported that water burst through the underground wash onto the surface just across the International Border. The border wall acted as a dam, keeping most of the flooding on the Mexican side. However, some water did flow through the port of entry into downtown Nogales, Arizona. Several businesses in the downtown business district experienced flooding and two illegal immigrants found two days later in the underground wash are also believed to have drowned due to this flooding. In addition, three illegal immigrants in an underground flood channel beneath the international border were rescued.

ADOT road weather sensor at San Simon measured a peak wind gust of 62 mph at 1303MST and a sustained wind speed of 42 mph at 1503MST. Visibility was reduced to between one quarter and one half mile in blowing dust at times.

The human caused Camino Fire started on April 20 near Sunizona in Cochise County as the result of a vehicle dragging tow chains along a roadway. The wildfire was driven by wind gusts to 45 mph at times and 750 acres were quickly burned before forward progression was stopped. The fire caused evacuations of around 40 residences, the closure of State Route 181, damage to utility infrastructure and the destruction of one structure. Fire suppression costs tallied $600,000.

Hot temperatures 15 degrees above normal, in the mid to upper 90s, were experienced on the Tohono O'odham Nation on April 18 causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert fifteen miles southwest of Topawa.

events.event_narrative: The human caused San Rafael Fire started on May 7 near the International Border in Santa Cruz County. The wildfire was driven by wind gusts to 45 mph at times and spread quickly in fine fuels along the Santa Cruz River north to the Canelo Hills, encompassing more than 10,000 acres by May 9. The fire caused evacuations of around 80 residences south of State Route 83, but no structures were damaged. The fire consumed 11,620 acres before becoming fully contained on May 15. Fire suppression costs tallied $2.5 million.

events.event_narrative: The extreme drought (D3) category was reached by mid May across Santa Cruz and southern Cochise Zones including the Huachuca, Mule, Dragoon and Chiricahua Mountains. Below normal precipitation occurred during the period of October 2021 through May 2022. Sierra Vista registered their 8th driest water year in over 120 years of record keeping with only 2.3 of rainfall through that period. Several human caused wildfires ignited in May and two grew rapidly due to dry fuels, including the Elgin Bridge and San Rafael fires.  Soil moisture readings were below normal, ranking below the 30th percentile.

The wildfire was driven by wind gusts to 35 mph at times and spread east quickly into the Mustang Mountains, encompassing 2,000 acres by the next day. The fire caused temporary evacuations of 11 residences, but no structures were damaged. The fire consumed 2149 acres before forward progress was stopped May 25.

The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for two individuals found in the desert, one north of San Miguel and another east of Sells.

Two to three inches of rainfall occurred in the border town of Lukeville, Arizona. This caused flooding and damage to private property, businesses and government offices with water several feet high. A report from officials at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument stated a recently built fence along the international border exacerbated the flooding as a result of the fence acting like a dam and stopping the normal progression of water through the border.

Extreme drought (D3) category continued across eastern Santa Cruz and southern Cochise counties including the Huachuca and Mule Mountains through June. Two wildfires ignited in dry fuels in the middle of the month. The Raspberry fire in the Chiricahua Mountains and the Tonto Canyon fire in western Santa Cruz County were both extinguished later in the month, in part due to two to three inches of rainfall. The late June rain was enough to reduce both areas, along with the Dragoon Mountains, to the severe drought (D2) category toward the end of June. Soil moisture readings improved to just above the 30th percentile across the area.

The lightning caused Raspberry Fire started on June 14 in the Chiricahua Mountains in Cochise County. Thunderstorm wind gusts of 30 mph helped the fire to quickly grow in mountainous terrain to more than 400 acres. The fire became fully contained on June 25, aided by several days of rainfall. Fire suppression costs for the 413 acre fire tallied just short of $1 million.

events.event_narrative: The Tonto Canyon Fire resulted from the combination of three fire starts near Manzanita Mountain in southwest Santa Cruz on June 12. The fire quickly grew to more than 4000 acres driven by wind gusts to 30 mph in dry fuels. Ruby Rd. was closed for a time as it was being used as a fire line. The fire consumed 9264 acres before becoming fully contained on June 22. About 3000 acres of this total were in Mexico. Fire suppression costs tallied $1.9 million.

The lightning caused Contreras Fire started on June 11 in the Baboquivari Mountains on Tohono O'odham tribal lands within Pima County. Gusty winds helped the fire grow rapidly in dry fuels and rugged terrain. Kitt Peak Observatory was evacuated prior to the fire overtaking the area on the 17th. One cabin, a dormitory and 1 shed were destroyed and the road was also damaged. Power poles were destroyed cutting off power to the observatory. Those damage estimates were near $500,000 but do not account for complete assessments of all telescopes and other equipment. The 20 residents of the community of Pan Tak were also temporarily evacuated as a precaution, but no damage occurred there. The fire became fully contained on June 24, aided by significant rainfall on the 23rd.  Fire suppression costs for the 29,482 acre fire tallied more than $13 million.

On the 12th, one was found in Tucson Mountain Park west of Tucson and another indoors within the City of Tucson.

An accident occurred near mile post 15 that involved a semi-tractor trailer which rolled onto its side. No injuries were reported.

Thunderstorm winds downed 42 power poles north of Douglas. The downed poles caused the closure of Highway 191 for 24 hours. More than 40 residences sustained at least minor roof or cosmetic damage. This included 5 mobile homes that either sustained major damage or were completely destroyed and 3 other residences that had substantial damage. Most of these were east of Leslie Canyon Dr. near Madrone Dr. where a microburst occurred. There were no injuries.
A peak gust of 59 mph was measured at KFHU Libby Field at 2013MST with 66 mph measured at KALK Pioneer Field at 2016MST.

Thunderstorm outflows from severe storms in Cochise County produced a peak wind gust of 77 mph at Canelo RAWS at 2030MST, 60 MPH at a CWOP station near Patagonia and 59 mph at KOLS Nogales Airport at 2044MST.
One inch diameter hail combined with wind gusts to 50 mph damaged sunflower crops north of Pearce.
A wind gust to 68 mph was recorded by a state DOT sensor at Olga and Interstate 10.
A wind gust to 60 mph was recorded by a state DOT sensor at Olga and Interstate 10.
Estimated thunderstorm wind gusts of 60 mph occurred southeast of Portal.  A Desert Research Institute sensor at Rodeo, NM observed a gust to 60 mph at 1900MST.
A thunderstorm wind gust to 59 mph measured at KALK Pioneer Field.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and rock slides across Route 80 northwest of Bisbee.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted trees near Greenock and Oracle Rd. in Oro Valley.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 1 hour near Tucson Mountain Park, caused flash flooding of several roads in Tucson Estates. Sheridan Ave. was washed out south of Kinney.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Dragoon Rd. south of Interstate 10.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused a rapid rise in Canada Del Oro Wash, causing the flooding and closure of Overton Rd.
Heavy rain of 3-4 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of Highway 85 near Puerto Blanco Dr. north of Lukeville.
Heavy rain of around 3 in 2 hours caused flash flooding of Highway 86 southeast of the Gu-Achi Trading Post. Santa Rosa Wash rose several feet north of Highway 86 but remained within its banks.
Guthrie RAWS measured a wind gust to 59 mph and large tree limbs were downed by thunderstorm winds in Clifton.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in the Clifton-Morenci area resulted in flash flooding and mud flows along Chase Creek which flooded Coronado Blvd. before flowing into the San Francisco River.

Thunderstorm winds produced a wall of dust that moved from near Santa Rosa north across northern Tohono O'odham Nation, eventually reaching Interstate 8 in Pinal County. Visibility was reduced to near zero, which stopped traffic along Route 15 north of Santa Rosa.

Heavy rain of 1-1.5 in less than 1 hour in the Broadway/Alvernon area led to rises in Arroyo Chico Wash. Crossings at Plumer Ave. and others were impassable. Additionally, a man on foot was swept away near 6th St. and 9th Ave.  He was rescued, but sustained minor injuries.

Heavy rain of 1-2 in 1 hour caused flash flooding of roadways in southeast Tucson. Road closures included Wilmot Rd. north of Noyes, Escalante Rd. at Atterbury Wash and Harrison Rd. at the Pantano Wash.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 2 hours over the Contreras Fire burn scar caused a 1-2 ft debris flow across State Highway 386 to Kitt Peak.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in 90 minutes over the Contreras Fire burn scar caused a 1-2 ft debris flow across State Highway 386 to Kitt Peak.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes in Aravaipa Canyon caused a debris flow and flash flood along the creek through the wilderness area.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in less than 2 hours over the Santa Catalina Mountains caused flash flooding in San Manuel and nearby areas with several dirt roads washed out.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 2 hours fell across the Rincon Mountains causing rises in Tanque Verde Creek that caused road closures of Wentworth Rd. and Tanque Verde Loop Rd.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines near Drexel and Calle Santa Cruz and downed large tree branches near Snyder and Bear Canyon Rds.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree near Tangerine and Lon Adams Rds.
Around 1 of heavy rain in less an 1 hour caused Valley View Wash to flood N. Flecha Dr. as well as River Rd. between Swan and Pontatoc Rds. in the Catalina Foothils.
Thunderstorm winds downed tree near 5th St. and Freeman Rd.
Thunderstorm winds downed a power line near Kenyon Dr and Gollob Rd.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused Gunsight Wash to rise rapidly and flood/close Highway 85 near mile post 55.
Heavy rain of 1 in less than 1 hour caused streets to become flooded and impassable in eastern portions of Nogales. Morley Ave. was closed at Madison St.

Heavy rain of 1-2 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of roadways from southeast to north central Tucson. Road closures included Escalante at Atterbury Wash, Harrison and Pantano Wash, Old Spanish Trail and Freeman Road, Bears Path Rd. south of Tanque Verde Road and Rudasill at Pima Wash.

Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 fell in less than 1 hour over the Finger Rock Canyon watershed with 2.29 recorded in 30 minutes at the Mt. Kimball gauge near the headwaters, which was in the severe burn area of the 2020 Bighorn Fire burn scar. Finger Rock Wash rose over 14 feet at a downstream gauge at the mouth of the canyon. Residents of seven homes and 12 people from another which was used as an assisted living facility were evacuated due to as much as 3 feet of water inside the structures.  Most of the structures will be purchased by the county and torn down. Several of the roads in the area were washed out and the wash structure itself was damaged.

Very hot high temperatures around 10 degrees above normal occurred on July 10 and 11, causing the High Heat Risk category to be reached. Ajo reached 114 degrees on the 10th and broke a record high on the 11th with 115 degrees while Organ Pipe National Monument reached 109. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found outdoors in Ajo on the 10th.

Very hot high temperatures around 10 degrees above normal occurred on July 11, causing the High Heat Risk category to be reached. Sells topped out at 109 degrees. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for two individuals found in the desert near Sells.

Very hot high temperatures around 10 degrees above normal occurred on July 11, causing the High Heat Risk category to be reached. The Tucson International Airport topped out at 110 degrees. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert south of Three Points.
Very hot high temperatures around 10 degrees above normal occurred on July 11, causing the High Heat Risk category to be reached. Picacho topped out at 110 degrees.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Hot high temperatures around 100 degrees, or 5 degrees above normal, occurred on July 11, causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert north of Nogales.

Hot high temperatures 100 to 105 degrees, or 5 degrees above normal, occurred on July 18, causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for two individuals found in the desert, one near Sells and another near Queen's Well.

Hot high temperatures around 105 degrees, or 5 degrees above normal, occurred on July 18, causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert near Three Points.

Hot high temperatures around 100 degrees, or 5 degrees above normal, occurred on July 18, causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert 30 miles northeast of Douglas.

Very hot high temperatures around 10 degrees above normal occurred across the lower elevations of southeast Arizona on July 22, causing the High Heat Risk category to be reached. The hottest temperature was 112 at Ajo. Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, Sells, Picacho, and Safford Airport (record) all topped out at 108 degrees.  Tucson International Airport reached 107.

Very hot high temperatures around 10 degrees above normal occurred across the lower elevations of southeast Arizona on July 22, causing the High Heat Risk category to be reached. The hottest temperature was 112 at Ajo. Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, Sells, Picacho, and Safford Airport (record) all topped out at 108 degrees.  Tucson International Airport reached 107.

The hottest temperature was 112 at Ajo. Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, Sells, Picacho, and Safford Airport (record) all topped out at 108 degrees.  Tucson International Airport reached 107.

The hottest temperature was 112 at Ajo. Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, Sells, Picacho, and Safford Airport (record) all topped out at 108 degrees.  Tucson International Airport reached 107.

The hottest temperature was 112 at Ajo. Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, Sells, Picacho, and Safford Airport (record) all topped out at 108 degrees.  Tucson International Airport reached 107.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 90 minutes caused flash flooding of roads and yards northwest of the intersection of Highway 90 and Route 82.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Route 80 northwest of Bisbee.
Several washes near the state prison in Fort Grant were flooded.
Thunderstorm winds downed several power poles on Gleeson Rd east of Tombstone causing a loss of power for 1100 customers. One home in Tombstone also sustained roof damage.
A wind gust of 58 mph was recorded at KSAD Safford Airport.

Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Davis Rd. east of Route 80 north of Bisbee. Flash flooding also occurred in Tombstone with the road washed out at the intersection of Ave. De La Loma & S. Laguna Ave.
Thunderstorm winds downed or snapped multiple power poles in the Elfrida and McNeal areas. One house, one barn and one garage also suffered substantial roof damage.
Gust to 64 mph was measured by Desert Research Institute sensor in northwest Chiricahua Mountains.
A thunderstorms outflow gust to 60 mph was measured at KTUS at 2110MST. A thunderstorm gust 60 mph was measured in east Tucson at 2123MST.
Heavy rain in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise in Nogales Wash, causing it to overtop its banks and flood the Doe St. Bridge.
Thunderstorm outflow winds resulted in a dust storm across south central Pinal County. Traffic on Interstate 10 was halted in both directions due to visibilities less than 100 feet.
Hail up to golf ball size fell in Sierra Vista. Hail broke a window in one home.
Two storms impacted Huachuca City with large hail.
Thunderstorm wind gusts to 70 and 74 mph, respectively were measured by two personal weather stations in Sierra Vista. A few trees were damaged by the winds.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 1 hour east of Saint David caused flash flooding in town. Homes were flooded near Cottonwood and Miller Lanes.
Nearly 1.5 of rain in 30 minutes on the Empire Mountains washed out Hilton Ranch Rd. which leads to the KEMX radar.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a tree near 6th St. and 6th Ave. in Tucson. The tree fell on top of a parked car.
Heavy rain of 1-2' in 1 hour in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise in Nogales Wash. The Doe St. bridge was overtopped and nearby roadways were flooded.
Thunderstorm winds downed multiple trees near Cortaro and Thornydale Rds. and downed power poles along Linda Vista Blvd.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Camino Verde Rd. near Bilby.
Heavy rain of 1-2 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and the closure of Tangerine Rd. between Interstate 10 and Twin Peaks Rd.
Heavy rain of 1.5 on the Bighorn burn scar caused rapid rises in Finger Rock Wash. Road closures resulted near Havasu Rd and Columbus Blvd and Pontatoc Rd. south of Skyline Dr.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding southeast of Three Points including Sierra Mountain Rd.

Heavy rain of 2-3 at the headwaters of Sabino Creek and Bear Canyon caused rapid rises in both streams. Flash flooding occurred at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area causing damage to trails and flooding of all recreation area bridges. Twenty five people became stranded in Bear Canyon and needed to be rescued as trails across the wash were flowing heavily and dangerously impassable. No injuries were reported.
A thunderstorm outflow boundary moved northwest along Interstate 10 lowering visibility to less than 1/4 mile from Picacho to Eloy.
Thunderstorm winds severely damaged an RV port and downed large tree limbs southwest of Mescal.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees near 6th St. and Euclid Ave. in Tucson.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour fell upstream to north of the Catalina Mountains in Pinal County. The Canada Del Oro Wash flowed over its banks south of Edwin Rd.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in Oracle caused extensive street flooding throughout the town.

Thunderstorm outflow winds produced a wall of dust that moved northeast across the far northern portion of the Tohono O'odham Nation in southwest Pinal County. Visibility was limited to less than one quarter mile along Route 15.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding in Pima, AZ.  Highway 70 became flooded and impassable.
Thunderstorms winds downed large limbs of several trees.
A thunderstorm wind gust to 60 mph was recorded at a Union Pacific weather station near Bowie.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding and road closures in Picture Rocks.  A school bus became stuck in floodwaters at Ina and Sandario Rds.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 caused flash flooding and road closures in southwest Tucson along Camino Verde as well as Old Ajo Hwy.
Heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in less than 2 hours caused flash flooding in Oro Valley and the closures of Overton and Hardy Roads and Linda Vista Blvd.
A funnel cloud formed briefily near Diamond Bell Ranch south of Three Points, AZ.

Two periods of heavy rain, each of 1 across much of the watershed, which was part of the Bighorn Fire burn scar, caused Sabino Creek to overtop bridges at the Sabino Canyon Recreation area. Some hiking trails, which were affected by high flows earlier in the month, sustained additional damage.
Upstream heavy rain of 1.5-2.5 in 2 hours caused Canada Del Oro Wash to flood part of N Lago Del Oro Parkway, resulting in its closure.
Heavy rain of 2 in 1 hour in the vicinity of Davis-Monthan AFB caused flash flooding and the closure of nearby roads including Contractors Way.

One inch of rain in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding near State Route 83 in the Lyle and Brushy Canyon areas south of Canelo.  Two occupants of a pickup truck were rescued from three feet of flowing water.
Rainfall of 1-1.5 in 3 hours caused sheet flooding and mud close portions of Gleason, Frontier and Davis Rds. near Elfrida and McNeal.

Heavy rain upstream in New Mexico caused the Gila River to flood at Duncan, AZ. Floodwaters caused the closure of Highway 70 and the temporary evacuation of a number of residents. Several homes and a couple businesses experienced minor flooding. The bakery near the corner of Highway 70 and Hill St. sustained the most significant damage from floodwaters. Levees between the river and the highway were damaged by the floodwaters.
Heavy rain in New Mexico caused elevated flows in the Gila River downstream as far as Solomon. Floodwaters partially flooded the bridge at Sanchez Rd. along with adjacent lowlands.

Thunderstorm winds downed 38 power poles and numerous trees along Kolb Rd. between Golf Links and Escalante Rds. The road remained closed for more than 24 hours to clean up the area prior to replacing all the poles.  At least 6000 customers were left without power.
A wind gust to 76 mph was recorded at KTUS Tucson Airport ASOS at 1834MST and a gust to 64 mph was recorded there at 1753MST. No damage was observed in the immediate vicinity.
Thunderstorms winds downed 8 power poles along Mission Rd.

Heavy rain of 2-2.5 in less than 90 minutes northeast of town caused flash flooding in St. David, mainly southwest of State Route 80, although the highway was closed due to flooding for a period of time. A total of 53 homes sustained at least some flood damage. A homeowner with a basement reported flood water hit a depth of 6 feet, destroying a new furnace and damaging electrical wiring. Floodwaters also affected septic tanks and wells.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in 1 hour caused flash flooding in southern Tucson. Swift water rescues from vehicles occurred near Bilby Rd. and Nogales Highway and Valencia Rd. and Park Ave.
A breach in the berm along Rucker Creek near Bell and Thompson Roads resulted in flash flooding of roadways near the creek in eastern sections of Elfrida.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in Elfrida and upstream of a breached berm along Rucker Creek caused flash flooding of streets in Elfrida. Yards also became flooded to the bases of houses.

Rainfall of 2 at the headwaters of Rucker Creek traveled downstream and through and existing breach in a berm combined with rainfall in the immediate area, resulted in an exacerbation of flooding in Elfrida. Flood waters expanded west of Highway 191 and became deeper throughout most of the community. A total of 42 residences sustained at least some flood damage. Eleven sustained major damage and 3 were determined to be a total loss. A couple of businesses also sustained flood damage and floodwaters also affected septic tanks and wells.

Heavy rain of more than 1 in 1 hour caused flash flooding and closures of residential streets south of Orange Grove Road between La Cholla and La Canada. Additionally, a man was rescued after becoming trapped under a bridge by floodwaters near Blacklidge and Walnut.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in Saguaro National Park and damage to Bajada Loop Rd.
A landspout was spotted near the Los Reales landfill on the south side of Tucson. It was nearly stationary before it dissipated.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 on Tucson's southeast side caused localized flash flooding. Escalante Rd. was closed at the Atterbury Wash and a man was rescued from his vehicle in the Alamo Wash at Yale Dr.
Heavy rain of 1-1.5 southeast of Valencia and Mission Rds. caused the West Branch of the Santa Cruz River to flood Drexel Road, causing its closure.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Hot high temperatures in the lower 90s, or 2 to 5 degrees above normal, occurred on August 29. This was just below the Moderate Heat Risk category. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert northeast of Ruby.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Hot high temperatures in the lower 90s, or 2 to 5 degrees above normal, occurred on August 30. This was just below the Moderate Heat Risk category. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert northeast of Kino Springs.
Heavy rain of 3-4 in three hours caused flash flooding and road closures in Green Valley, including Camino Del Sol and Abrego Drive.
Thunderstorm wind downed 3 power poles south of North Komelik.
Thunderstorm winds downed large tree limbs in Saddlebrooke.
Heavy rain of 2-3 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in southwest Tucson. Roads closed include Old Ajo Highway, Long Cast DR. and Iberia Ave.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines on Sanders Rd. causing its closure and the lost of power for more than 2000 customers. Winds also downed several Palo Verde trees near  Moore Rd.
Heavy rain of an inch in one hour caused flash flooding near Agua Caliente Park and the closure of Soldier Trail Rd. near Roger Rd.
Pioneer Field KALK ASOS recorded a thunderstorm wind gust to 58 mph.

A lightning strike at Agua Caliente Park on the northeast side of the Tucson Metro area ignited a blaze that damaged 225 palm trees and 40 other trees. The fire also damaged signs, picnic tables, trash cans, a bike rack, and parts of irrigation systems. About 40 palm trees were so severely burned they were removed. The park remained closed for 60 days.

Hot high temperatures around 105 degrees, or 4 to 6 degrees above normal, occurred on September 5 causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert near Route 1 in the far western part of the Tohono O'odham Nation.
About a foot of snow occurred near the summit of Mt. Lemmon at elevations above 8000 feet.
About a foot of snow occurred near the summit of Mt. Graham at elevations above 8000 feet.
Scout Camp RAWS measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph.
Thunderstorm winds downed a few trees in Midvale Park in the southwest Tucson metro area. One of the trees fell onto a residence, causing minor damage.
Horse Camp RAWS measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 59 mph.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: About 12 of snow occurred in the higher elevations of northern Greenlee County in the Hannagan Meadow area.
At the Mount Graham observatory, about 12 of snow occurred.
Lightning struck a power pole along Route 15 just north of Highway 86. The pole caught fire and caused a power outage on the Tohono O'odham Nation that persisted for three hours.
About 19 inches of snow occurred in the Summerhaven region of Mt. Lemmon.
Mount Graham observatory reported 12 to 24 inches of snow on the summit of Mount Graham.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: The SNOTEL near Hanngan Meadow recorded about 18 of snow.
Satellite estimates (in line with other mountain ranges) indicated that greater than 12 of snow occurred at the higher peaks of the Chiricahua Mountains.
Satellite estimates (in line with other mountain ranges) indicated that greater than 12 of snow occurred at the higher peaks of the Huachuca Mountains.

Sustained southwest winds of 40 mph and gusts greater than 60 mph were observed in the Sierra Vista area. KALK Pioneer Field measured a gust to 66 mph at 1039MST and 1109MST while KFHU Libby Field measured a gust to 63 mph at 1038MST. Two power poles were downed along Cherokee Ave. south of Buffalo Soldier Trail.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: Strong wind gusts of 30 to 50 mph combined with snowfall totals of 6 to 12 inches occurred over the White Mountains of Graham and Greenlee Counties.
Strong wind gusts of 30 to 50 mph combined with snowfall totals of 6 to 12 inches occurred over the White Mountains of Graham and Greenlee Counties.
Strong wind gusts of 30 to 50 mph combined with snowfall totals of 6 to 12 inches occurred over the Santa Catalina Mountains including Summerhaven and Mount Lemmon.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: Wind gusts in excess of 60 mph were common across the White Mountains along with a storm total of 6 to 12 inches of snow with blizzard-like conditions at times. Portions of Highway 191 were closed.

Wind gusts in excess of 60 mph were common across the Gailuro Mountains including Mount Graham along with a storm total of 6 to 12 inches of snow with blizzard-like conditions at times. Route 366 was closed.

Wind gusts in excess of 60 mph were common across the Santa Catalina Mountains along with a storm total of 12 to 14 inches of snow with blizzard-like conditions at times. Several trees and power poles were down on Mt, Lemmon prompting Ski Valley to close down their slopes the following day to assess repairs.
A trained spotter reported water flowing over Ramsey Road near Hereford.
A trained spotter reported flooding on Highway 191 near Pearce.

Heavy rainfall from thunderstorms across the Santa Catalina Mountains took 8 to 10 h ours to move downstream into the Rillito River. A woman drove into the river at a non barricaded crossing and was swept partially downstream. This person was successfully rescued from the flowing stream.
The Pantano Wash at Vail crested at 12.6 feet or 1.6 feet above bankful at 9:00 PM.
A trained spotter reported nickel sized hail in Sahuarita.
An 18 year old man was struck by lightning and injured while working on the roof of a house.
A trained spotter reported 0.90 inch of rain in 15 minutes with roadways flooded in the Sahuarita area.
Roof was partially blown off a home near 22nd and Camino Seco in Tucson.
Law enforcement reported water flowing over Charleson Road near Tombstone.
A car was flooded in the roadway near Grant Road and Alvernon Road in Tucson.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: About 4 of snow fell in the Patagonia area with gusts as high as 60 mph immediately preceding the changeover to snow.
About 5 inches of snow fell in the Saddlebrooke area and 6 inches in Oracle resulting in difficult travel, especially on secondary roadways.

About 4 to 5 inches of snow fell in the Benson area with 4 inches  in the Tombstone area, resulting in difficult driving conditions. One to four inches in the Sierra Vista area caused schools to be closed for the day.

events.cz_name: UPPER GILA RIVER AND ARAVAIPA VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: About 4 inches of snow fell in the Klondyke area resulting in difficult travel, especially on secondary roadways.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: About 10 to 12 inches of snow occurred in the Hannagan Meadow area with wind gusts in excess of 50 mph.
About 12 inches of snow occurred on Mount Graham with wind gusts in excess of 50 mph.
About 4 inches of snow occurred in the Paradise area and Rucker had a wind gust to 55 mph.

About 6 to 12 inches of snow occurred in the higher elevations of the Dragoon, Mule, Huachuca and Santa Rita Mountains, accompanied by strong winds. A gust to 67 mph was recorded south of Patagonia at 6200 ft MSL.
About 12 inches of snow occurred in Summerhaven with wind gusts in excess of 50 mph.
Heavy rainfall occurred at Coronado National Memorial causing flash flooding as washes overflowing the roadway causing significant damage.
Thunderstorm winds downed a shallow-rooted tree which fell onto a mobile home, causing significant roof and wall damage.

A prolonged rain event on Jan 15 and 16 produced 1 to 3 inches of rain across the Tucson Metro area and adjacent foothills. Rising waters caused the closure of numerous roads at  low water crossings. Water rescues from flowing channels occurred including one in Arroyo Chico near Kino Parkway and another in the Santa Cruz River near Prince Rd. About 300 campers were stranded in Catalina St. Park when their egress from the park was cut off by flood waters.

Temperatures fell into the teens during the morning of February 16 with wind chills in the single digits. While air temperatures were not as cold for the next 24 hours, winds increased to 20 to 30 mph with gusts of 50 to 60 mph and created wind chills as cold as the teens into the morning of February 17. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that the primary cause of death was hypothermia for two individuals found in the Santa Rita Mountains.
Sustained winds were measured at 40 mph in the Sierra Vista area with the KALK ASOS reporting 40 mph at 1156MST.
A wind gust to 67 mph was measured at a site near Patagonia at 6200 feet MSL at 2345MST.
A peak wind gust of 61 mph was recorded at Horse Camp Canyon RAWS at 1002MST.

Several trees were uprooted in Sierra Vista where at least one home sustained moderate roof damage. Winds peeled shingles off a garage near Benson. A peak wind gust of 68 mph was recorded at KALK Pioneer Airfield ASOS at 1006MST and 64 mph at KFHU Libby Field ASOS at 1009MST. Sustained winds between 40 and 45 mph were measured at KALK and KFHU ASOS locations.

Sustained winds between 40 and 45 mph were recorded at several DOT weather stations along I-10 with a peak gust of 70 mph measured at San Simon at 1133MST. Blowing dust reduced visibilities to less than a quarter mile at times. KDUG ASOS near Douglas recorded a peak wind gust of 63 mph at 1337MST. At a farm near Willcox, winds pulled a large, anchored canopy tent out of the ground, destroying it and damaging a nearby house deck to which it was fastened. Winds downed power lines in the Sunizona area.

events.cz_name: UPPER GILA RIVER AND ARAVAIPA VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Guthrie RAWS at 6300 ft MSL recorded several gusts higher than 65 mph and a peak gust of 92 mph at 1203MST.  A portable RAWS at 4800 ft MSL near the Galiuro Mountains recorded a gust to 65 mph at 1128MST.
A Desert Research Institute station at 6800 ft MSL in the Chiricahua Mountains measured a gust to 65 mph at 1020MST and 66 mph at 1410MST.

High winds bent and downed a commercial radio communication tower 90 degrees at Juniper Flats (7700 ft MSL) in the Mule Mountains. A weather station at about 5400 ft MSL near Bisbee measured a peak gust of 71 mph at 1048MST.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: A peak wind gust of 62 mph was recorded at a private weather station at 4000 ft MSL near Patagonia at 1030MST and the KOLS Nogales ASOS measured a peak gust to 59 mph at 1053MST.
Strong winds downed power lines near Interstate 19 and Pima Mine Road south of Tucson, causing a closure of the northbound lanes for more than 2 hours.
Strong winds downed a tree in Sells. The tree fell on a house causing minor damage.

Cold temperatures below 15 degrees during the early morning hours of February 16 caused several well heads to freeze, causing damage to some in eastern Cochise County. |Record low temperatures were observed at the Bisbee-Douglas Airport (12 degrees) and San Simon (13 degrees).

High winds occurred across eastern Cochise County from the afternoon of March 1 to just past midnight. The peak gust of 63 mph was measured at San Simon at 0103MST. Bisbee-Douglas KDUG ASOS recorded a 61 mph gust the previous afternoon at 1508MST.
A peak wind gust to 61 mph was recorded at Bisbee-Douglas Airport KDUG ASOS at 1430MST with a 58 mph gust at San Simon at 1403MST.
Tombstone Police Department reported penny size hail.

The human caused Williams Fire started on April 3 in the Hereford area in Cochise County.  The wildfire was driven by wind gusts of 45 mph, spread northeast in dry grass, and destroyed two residences and three outbuildings near the intersection of Williams and Waters Rds. The fire caused evacuations of several residences and the closure of State Route 92. A total of 1320 acres were burned. Forward progression was stopped on April 4. Fire suppression costs tallied $90,000.

In the Sulphur Springs Valley of northern Cochise and southern Graham counties, temperatures remained below 20 degrees for several hours from midnight to 7 am with a low temperature of 14 degrees. This late season hard freeze caused the total loss of the cherry and peach crops with a 90 percent loss of the apple and pear crops as the fruit was in full bloom at the time. Early crop pistachios were entirely lost.

events.event_narrative: In the Sulphur Springs Valley of northern Cochise and southern Graham counties, temperatures remained below 20 degrees for several hours from midnight to 7 am with a low temperature of 14 degrees. The fires spread rapidly due to gusty winds with two fires combining to form the Wildhorse Fire. State Route 92 was closed for a time and residents of Three Canyons development were temporarily evacuated. While burning in a residential area, no houses were damaged, although four small outbuildings were destroyed. The fire consumed a total of 747 acres before becoming fully contained June 24. events.event_narrative: The human caused Beehive Fire started during the evening of June 30 north of Ruby Road in Santa Cruz County. Due to hot and dry conditions in early July, the fire spread to 300 acres on July 1, to 3000 acres in the rugged terrain of Beehive Canyon by July 3 and topped 10,000 acres by July 8 as it entered extreme southeast Pima County. The fire consumed 10,745 acres before becoming fully contained on July 12. Fire suppression costs tallied nearly $5 million. The much smaller Beehive 2 Fire spotted just south of the Beehive Fire on July 8 and was aggressively suppressed, with costs tallying another $7 million.

Two lightning caused fires started at nearly the same time on July 19 on either side of Interstate 10 west of Dragoon in Cochise County. Both fires were spread by thunderstorm winds on July 20. The Robles Fire to the south of I-10, which consumed 3000 acres, was contained on July 22 with fire suppression costs tallying over $600,000. The Adams Peak Fire, which consumed 2232 acres to the north of I-10, was contained on July 23 with fire suppression costs of $500,000.

The lightning caused Bowl Creek Fire started July 23 west of Oracle Junction in Pinal County. Due to windy and dry conditions, the fire quickly spread to 1000 acres. It consumed a total of 1156 acres before full containment was achieved on July 26.  Fire suppression costs tallied $100,000.

A total of 14 heat-related fatalities were reported by the Pima County Medical Examiner. Heat was determined to be the primary cause of death for two individuals found in the desert, one near Three Points on the 12th and another in the Ironwood Forest National Monument on the 13th. Heat was also found to the primary cause of death for four individuals in Tucson. Two individuals were found on the 13th on Tucson streets and subsequently died at the hospital. Another was found deceased outdoors on the 13th and a fourth died on the 12th in their home where the A/C had been turned off. Heat was found to be a contributing factor in the deaths of 8 individuals in Tucson. Two persons died in their homes in which the A/C unit was either broken or turned off. They both also had complicating factors of heart disease. Six others were found outside at various locations in the city. The complicating factor for four of them was drug toxicity, while the other two suffered from other health issues.

Heat was determined to be a contributing factor for an elderly man with other health issues who died in his front yard in Rio Rico in July 21.

A total of 40 heat-related fatalities were reported by the Pima County Medical Examiner. Heat was determined to be the primary cause of death for 13 individuals in Tucson, one in Oro Valley, and one near Sahuarita. Seven of these deaths occurred outdoors while eight individuals were found indoors with A/C units which were either not working, turned off or not present at all. Heat was determined to be a contributing factor for 25 individuals, in Tucson or the immediate vicinity. Twelve of these included the complicating factor of drug toxicity (10 outdoors and 2 indoors with a nonfunctioning A/C). Ten in Tucson suffered from various health issues (2 outdoors and 8 indoors with a nonfunctioning A/C). Heat was a contributing factor for an additional three individuals who had other health issues, one each in Green Valley, Sahuarita and Vail.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Cold low temperatures in the high single digits to teens, or 15 to 25 degrees below normal, occurred in Patagonia with the lowest temperature of 9 degrees recorded the morning of January 24. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined that hypothermia was the primary cause of death for two individuals in Patagonia. One individual lived in a mobile home that did not have sufficient heating was found there on the floor January 23. They were transported to a hospital but died there that day. A second individual was found deceased outside their home on January 24.

Low temperatures in the mid to upper 20s with wind chills near 20 degrees resulted in cold that was 15 to 20 degrees below the normal low temperature for February 6. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined that hypothermia was the primary cause of death for a homeless individual who had ingested methamphetamines and was found outdoors in downtown Tucson. The individual was transported to a hospital, but died later that day.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Hot temperatures 7 to 15 degrees above normal caused the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached in Santa Cruz County where temperatures below 5000 feet topped out in the 90s. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined heat to be the primary cause of death for two individuals found in the desert; one near Amado and another north of Patagonia.

Hot temperatures 11 to 14 degrees above normal caused the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached in western Pima County where temperatures topped out between 100 and 105 degrees. A record high temperature of 103 degrees occurred at Ajo. The Pima County Medical Examiner determined heat to be the primary cause of death for one individual found in the desert west of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument.
A 7 foot rise occurred on the Nogales Wash in Nogales.
Several streets were flooded in Sierra Vista with 0.75 inches of rain reported in 15 minutes.
Power lines were blown down and a roof was reported blown off a house in Sells.
Power outages were reported in Ajo as a result of power lines being down.

Numerous reports of flash flooding occurred in Tucson including one to two feet of water flowing on 5th street and Alvernon Way, a driver pulled from a car due to rising water at Stone and Mabel streets. 1.10 inches of rain occurred in 10 minutes near Country Club and Pima Roads with streets flooded.
Trained spotter reported penny size hail at River and Swan.

Extensive wind damage occurred on the north side of Tucson due to a microburst. Damage reported included 28 power poles knocked down including a dozen at River Road and Dodge Blvd resulting in 35,000 customers without power, some for an extended period as much as two days. Damage was also reported at the Jewish Community Center near River Road and Alvernon Way. There was also roof damage to numerous businesses and hundreds of trees knocked down.
A tree was reported downed near Broadway and Tucson Blvd.
There was at least two feet of water flowing at Alamo Wash at Glenn Ave from a second round of rainfall per the Pima County Flood Control District Stream gage.
A trained spotter reported one inch of rainfall occurred in 30 minutes in Vail with streets flooded.
A swift water rescue occurred along Wentworth Road.
A swift water rescue occurred at a wash in Sells where two people needed to be rescued.

Several roads were flooded in the Bisbee and Hereford area due to heavy rainfall. In addition tons of gravel, rock and debris from the slopes of Zacatecas Canyon turned Brewery Gulf in Bisbee into a river. Trained spotters in Hereford reported two inches of rain in 45 minutes and 2.25 inches of rain in 75 minutes.

The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of one individual on the Tohono O'odham Nation along a walking path.

The extreme (D3) drought category across far southern and eastern sections of southeast Arizona ended on April 22. This area near the New Mexico line encompassed southern Greenlee, southeast Graham and eastern Cochise counties, including the Chiricahua Mountains.||A storm system resulted in rain across the region on April 1 and this rain in combination with winter rainfall was enough to move the area from extreme (D3) drought category to severe (D2) drought category.

Measured wind gust to 61 mph at Pioneer Airfield.

Several rounds of thunderstorms moved over the Pima area from 6 PM until after 10 PM in the evening. This caused extensive street flooding and flash flooding with water running curb to curb on numerous streets.
Numerous large trees downed along with a railroad crossing arm damaged due to severe wind gusts in Pima, AZ.

Several severe threshold wind gusts occurred at the Tucson International Airport with the strongest wind gust of 73 mph. This strong wind also caused a dust storm with visibility less than one quarter of a mile. Numerous trees were also reported down on the south side per broadcast media.

Thunderstorms brought heavy intense rainfall over the Tucson Metro area. Rainfall totals ranged from 1 to 2.5 inches from Pima County Alert Gauges. ||Tucson Fire Department responded to over 25 calls with 15 of those calls relating to stranded drivers or stuck in swift moving water. Two adults were found dead in a wash after a swift water rescue attempt.

Many reports of downed trees across the city of Tucson. Estimated wind gusts of 45 mph. Likely scenario is that winds were strong enough combined with saturated ground due to very heavy rain to result in many trees being downed.
The Canelo RAWS site recorded a wind gust of 70 mph.
The Mt. Hopkins RAWS measured a wind gust to 78 mph.
Heavy rain, estimated at 2 to 3 inches caused flash flooding along Central Highway north of Highway 80.
Mesonet station at Cochise College airport recorded a wind gust of 58 mph.
The Nogales Wash at Nogales exceeded bankfull at about 8 feet causing flooding in the Morley Road region of Nogales.
A thunderstorm on the east side of Tucson produced a wind gust strong enough to uproot a large Palo Verde tree.  This was near Pantano Rd and Seneca St. Time estimate based on radar.
The Tucson International Airport recorded a gust to 58 mph.
Large palo verde tree uprooted and 8 foot saguaro snapped at base. Time estimated via radar.
A personal weather station via weather underground reported a wind gust to 58 mph.
A wind gust of 72 mph occurred at Pioneer Airfield on Fort Huachuca.
CWOP weather station CW4232 recorded a wind gust of 60 mph.
A wind gust of 58 mph was recorded near Saint David.
Two weather stations in San Simon recorded wind gusts to 66 mph and 62 mph, respectively.
Numerous trees reported down in the areas of Oracle Rd and Wetmore Rd in Tucson and near Euclid St and Waverly in Tucson.

A tornado with a maximum intensity of EF-1 developed in the vicinity of the Amazon Fulfillment Center near Kolb Road and Valencia Road. The tornado tracked towards the east-southeast, generally parallel to Valencia Road, and ended near Valencia Road and Frost Drive. Damage along the tornado path included many downed, snapped and uprooted trees, roof damage (primarily to tiles). Additionally, a large shipping container was moved and flipped on its side. The shipping container damaged a chain-link fence. ||Damage consistent with EF-1 rating was just south of Valencia Road near Old Vail Road and included large trees uprooted. Maximum estimated winds are 100 mph.

A dry microburst resulted in 14 downed power poles were destroyed, multiple falling into on coming traffic, of which two power poles landed on cars injuring and trapping people inside, and significantly damaging the cars. Significant power outages resulted in over 1000 costumers without power for an extended amount of time. The Utility company (TEP) reported taking 4 to 5 days to rebuild their infrastructure as a result of the impacts.

Hot temperatures around 6 degrees above normal were experienced in the Tucson Metro Area May 18 causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. Tucson International Airport topped out at 99 degrees. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was a contributing factor in the death of one individual.

Tucson International Airport topped out at 108 degrees on June 6 and 109 degrees on June 7, which tied the daily record. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was a contributing factor in the death of one individual on June 7.

Very hot temperatures about 6 degrees above normal. A high temperature of 101 occurred in Pearce-Sunsites on June 10 with Moderate Heat Risk. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of one individual found outside near their residence in Elfrida on June 10.

Hot temperatures 6 to 9 degrees above normal were experienced in the Tucson Metro Area June 11 and June 12, causing the Major Heat Risk category to be reached. The high temperature in Tucson was 108 degrees on June 11 and 109 on June 12. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of one individual found in their residence in Tucson on June 11 and a contributing factor in the death of another individual on June 11.

The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of one individual found in the desert near Topawa.

The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of one individual found in the desert near Ajo.

Hot temperatures about 3 to 6 degrees above normal were experienced in eastern Pima County on June 23, causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. Tucson had a high of 101 degrees on June 23. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was a contributing factor in the death of one individual located in a parking lot in Tucson.

Hot temperatures 3 to 6 degrees above normal were experienced in eastern Cochise County June 25, causing the Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached. The high in Douglas was 99 degrees. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of two individuals found near Douglas.

The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of one individual located in their residence in Tucson.

Ajo topped out at 108 and 109 degrees on June 26 and 27 with a low temperature of 85 degrees. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary factor in the death of three individuals found in the desert near Ajo. Two of those were on June 26 and the other on June 27.
