events.event_narrative: The higher elevations of Graham and Greenlee County received 6 to 12 inches of snow combined with wind gusts in excess of 50 MPH, which caused brief blizzard-like conditions. This event began on January 31.

Strong wind in the Tucson area damaged two substations and downed power lines. The result was the loss of power to 54,000 customers for 2 to 4 hours. Service was restored to most customers by 1 am MST on February 1st.  A large tree was also downed by the winds near the Reid Park Zoo.
Strong wind in the Tucson area resulted in numerous power outages with power poles and wires down in a few spots across the city.
A wind gust to 75 MPH was recorded with 5 inches of snow on Mt. Hopkins observatory.  Power lines were also knocked down near Bisbee.  This event continued into February 1.
A wind gust to 75 MPH was recorded with 5 inches of snow on Mt. Hopkins observatory. Power lines were also knocked down near Bisbee. This event began on January 31.
Wind gusts in excess of 40 MPH occurred on Mt. Graham in addition to 7 inches of snow. This event continued into February 1.
Wind gusts in excess of 40 MPH occurred on Mt. Graham in addition to 7 inches of snow. This event began on January 31.

Heavy rain of generally between 0.50 and 1.25 inches during the afternoon of January 7 caused multiple road closures across Pima County, including parts of the Tucson metro. One car stalled near the intersection of Lee St. and Santa Rosa Ave in approximately 6 inches of water during the rush hour. About 12 hours later, 2 people became stranded in their vehicle after it became stuck in a running wash on Limberlost Road just west of Soldier Trail just before dawn on January 8. No injuries or fatalities occurred.

Southwest winds gusting up to 45 mph blew dust from an non-maintained parcel of land adjacent to Interstate 10 across the roadway causing near-zero visibility during the afternoon hours. The result was a collision involving two tractor-trailers heading westbound near Mile Post 376, about 15 miles west of the New Mexico/Arizona state line. Both vehicles and their payloads sustained substantial damage. Sixty miles of interstate were closed for about 2 hours due to both blowing dust to the collision.

Interstate 10 was closed for 2 periods during the afternoon due to blowing dust causing near-zero visibility. The first closure was for approximately 1 hour, from 3 to 4 pm, between Mile Post 352 and 378. The second closure was once again from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from approximately 5 pm through 8 pm. No accidents were reported.

Blowing dust once again originating from an non-maintained parcel of land adjacent to Interstate 10 caused near-zero visibility during the early afternoon hours. This resulted in 3 collisions involving a total of 12 vehicles within a mile of Mile Post 376. The vehicles involved included a San Simon fire truck as well as a DPS SUV. No serious injuries were reported, as the DPS officer was 50 ft away from his vehicle when it was struck by a semi, and the fire chief had also exited his vehicle when impact occurred. The interstate was closed, from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from 2 pm through 7 pm in both directions for a total of 60 miles. Traffic was rerouted along State Route 191/70 through Safford, AZ, a detour of approximately 110 miles. Winds were from the southwest with gusts to between 35 and 40 mph at the time of the collisions.

Strong southwest winds of 45 to 55 mph damaged the roofs of several apartments in the 800 block of Eighth Street between C and D Avenues in Douglas. The units were determined unsafe to live in until repairs could be made.

Southwest winds gusting up to 30 mph blew dust from an non-maintained parcel of land adjacent to Interstate 10 across the roadway causing near-zero visibility during the afternoon hours. The result was a two vehicle accident near Mile Post 376, about 15 miles west of the New Mexico/Arizona state line. Sixty miles of interstate were closed for about 2 hours due to both blowing dust to the collision.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted trees in rural Santa Cruz County.

Blowing dust limited visibilities to near zero along Interstate 10 near Milepost 376 from late morning into early evening. The interstate was preemptively closed from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from approximately 10 am through 7 pm. Thus, no accidents occurred.

Blowing dust limited visibilities to near zero along Interstate 10 near Milepost 376 for much of the afternoon. This prompted the closing of the interstate from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from approximately 2 pm through 6 pm. No accidents occurred.

Blowing dust limited visibilities to near zero along Interstate 10 near Milepost 376 for much of the afternoon. This prompted the closing of the interstate from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from approximately 1 pm through 4 pm. No accidents occurred.

Blowing dust limited visibilities to near zero along Interstate 10 near Milepost 376 late in the day. This prompted the closing of the interstate from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from approximately 6 pm through 8 pm. No accidents occurred.

Blowing dust limited visibilities to near zero along Interstate 10 near Milepost 376 for much of the day. This prompted the closing of the interstate from Lordsburg, NM to Willcox, AZ from approximately 2 pm through 6 pm. No accidents occurred.

Facebook reports from the public indicated a measured 64 mph wind gust at Safford Ranch. One large tree was uprooted and fell on a vehicle. The Safford Electric Division reported power lines snapped and 3 or 4 poles had to be replaced. A chain linked fence was blown over.
Multiple reports and photos of trees uprooted and broken branches on the northwest side of Tucson. Some branches fell on vehicles. Wind damage to a church roof led to extensive water damage inside.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a fence and snapped 4 tree branches on the northwest side of Tucson.
A home on the 1700 block of S. Avenida Regulo was damaged when a lightning strike caused a fire. The residents were not home at the time and no was was injured.
City of Tucson reported a lightning strike to a home near 22nd St and Kolb Rd.

Multiple reports from just east of the University of Arizona campus to near River Road and Campbell of large trees uprooted, limbs snapped, and power lines down. The roof of Covenant Generations church on Tucson Blvd was severely damaged. Trees fell on carports and homes in the Winterhaven area of town. Severe damage was sustained at the Campbell Ranch Apartments as trees fell on buildings and vehicles. Major tree damage occurred at Himmel Park. For some residents, power was not restored until noon on June 27th. One person was electrocuted after coming in contact with a live downed wire but survived.
Weather station near Picacho Peak recorded a 65 mph wind gust.

Multiple swift water rescues within the midtown area. A family of 4 became stranded near Lee St. and 9th Ave when their vehicle stalled in flood waters up to their windshield. Other rescues were needed when vehicles traveling through roads covered in water became inoperable. Rainfall amounts of 0.50 inches in 15 minutes occurred, with storm total amounts of up to 2 inches across parts of the metro.
Thunderstorm winds damaged roofs northeast of Ryan Field. Large trees were uprooted near San Joaquin Rd and Bopp Rd, as well as Kinney Rd and SR86.
Willcox Range News reported that the storm blew the roof off the bleachers at the Quail Park Rodeo grounds northwest of Willcox.
Horse Camp RAWS recorded a 58 mph wind gust.

Very hot temperatures over a four-day stretch contributed to at least 14 serious heat-related illnesses in Eastern Pima County alone.  A 72-year old man was airlifted to the hospital after he suffered heat exhaustion on Tanque Verde Falls hiking trail on June 3rd. Tucson International Airport tied a record high of 107 degrees on June 3rd, and set new records of 110 on June 5th and 111 on June 6th, respectively.  Organ Pipe National Monument set new record highs of 111 on June 3rd and 114 on June 5th. Temperatures during the period were as hot as 108 in Oracle and Sasabe, 109 in the Sierra Vista/Benson area and 112 in Sells.

A three-day stretch of very hot temperatures resulted in four heat-related fatalities and at least 19 heat-related illnesses in southeast Arizona, all of which were reported in Eastern Pima County. Out of three men who were hiking the Ventana Canyon Trail Sunday, June 19th, two died of heat stroke, although one was not found until Tuesday. The third man suffered heat-related injuries but survived.  A woman died of heat stoke that same day hiking Finger Rock Trail. Her companion was airlifted to a hospital for treatment of heat-related illness. Also on that same day, a woman walking the city's Loop walking and biking trail succumbed to heat stroke near Interstate 10 and Irvington.  Tucson International Airport recorded its third hottest day ever and the warmest day since 1994 with a record setting 115 degrees on June 19th. Other record highs on the 19th included 115 degrees at Picacho Peak, 119 at Organ Pipe National Monument, 112 at Safford and 109 at Nogales and Bisbee-Douglas Airport. On June 20th, additional record highs were set although the actual temperatures were not quite as hot.

On June 20th, additional record highs were set although the actual temperatures were not quite as hot.
A 58 mph wind gust occurred at the Black Hills RAWS.
Nickel size hail fell at Garigan's Gulch and Rincon Mesa Drive in Vail.

Over 60-water related calls and road closures occurred, mainly within metro Tucson, due to up to 2.5 inches of rainfall. A swift water rescue occurred at Elm St near Tucson Blvd. The Stone Street Underpass was closed for several hours with up to 8 feet of standing water and a stalled vehicle. Vehicles also stalled in water in the Orange Grove Road underpass. Many surface streets were running with a foot or more of water. A daily record of 0.83 inches of rain fell at Tucson International Airport.
Tucson Fire Dept reported a tree struck by lightning caught fire on the corner of Drexel Rd and Mission Rd.

Thunderstorm outflow winds created a wall of dust that resulted in a multi-vehicle accident at milepost 214 on I-10 near Picacho Peak. Two separate crashes involving a total of 7 vehicles occurred, involving 3 and 4 vehicles each. Visibility was reduced below 1/2 mile, and I-10 was closed in both directions for approximately 20 minutes. The closure caused a 1 mile backup in either direction. No injuries were reported.
Thunderstorm wind gust of 61 mph recorded at Hopkins RAWS.
Thunderstorm outflow winds knocked down a tree on Forbes Blvd near Grant and I-10.
Hopkins RAWS reported a 59 mph wind gust.
A lightning strike caused a house fire in the 10100 block of East Karen place around 930 pm. No one was injured.

A line of thunderstorms moved southwest pushing strong winds out ahead of it through Redington Pass and into the Tucson Metro. Wind gusts of 60 to 65 mph caused sporadic damage.  Ten power poles and several trees were knocked down near Camino Seco and Escalante Rd. Over 19,000 customers were without power for a short time. Additionally, a carport was damaged near Escalante Rd and Prudence Rd, and a tree fell on a home on Rickey Vista in South Tucson.
Thunderstorm wind gusts were measured at KSAD ASOS to 51 kts and at Black Hills RAWS to 50 kts.
A 69 mph gust occurred at the Horse Camp RAWS.

A line of thunderstorms pushed northwest through Tucson. Wind damage occurred at an Eegee's restaurant at Thornydale Rd and Ina Rd, and a large tree was blown down nearby. Additionally, a shed was blown over into a fence. Other trees were blown down at Ina Rd and Mona Lisa Dr, near the CDO bike path near Magee Rd, and on Eaglestone Loop near Hartman Ln.
Flood waters swept a vehicle into the Sikul Himatk Wash on the Tohono O'Odham Nation. The motorist escaped to dry land.
The Tohono O'Odham Nation dispatch reported an ongoing swift water rescue approximately 4 miles north of SR 86 on Indian Route 35. A motorist was trapped in their vehicle.
Thunderstorm winds blew a roof off a home and damaged trees and power lines in the Royal Road area of Nogales.
Thunderstorm winds pushed a storage container 2 feet, blew the door off the mobile home and blew down a nearby shed.

Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in parts of Benson. Benson Middle School was most severely impacted by flood waters. Water was at least ankle deep in an entire wing of the school, damaging rugs and floorboards in ten classrooms. The city of Benson Public Works Building also sustained minor flood damage.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines in Sahuarita that left 1300 customers without power.
Heavy rainfall measured at nearly 3.5 inches caused flash flooding near Interstate 10 and Kolb Rd. Three vehicles became stranded in flood waters but no injuries occurred.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Highway 80 northwest of Bisbee.

Heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches in a short time flooded several roads in southwest Cochise County including Moson Road near Hereford, Charleston Rd between Sierra Vista and Tombstone and Davis Rd between Tombstone and McNeal.
Spotter estimates thunderstorm wind gust of 60 mph north of Sunsites.
Gusty thunderstorm outflow winds destroyed a metal silo. The winds moved the nearly empty silo about 60 feet.

A slow-moving thunderstorm moved through Oro Valley, causing extensive wind damage. The strongest winds snapped three power poles  along Hardy Rd near La Canada. A tree 12 inches in diameter was broken in half at the base on Magee Rd between La Cholla Rd and La Canada Rd and widespread tree damage occurred near CDO High School, the Oro Valley Aquatic Center and at numerous residences. Around 2000 TEP customers were without power for portions of the night and into the early morning hours.

Heavy rain caused washes to overtop secondary roads between Kearny and Florence. A |32-yr old man attempted to drive his truck across a wash near Whitlow Ranch and Hawkview Roads and became stuck when water rushed into his vehicle.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding and 3 swift water rescues on the periphery of the Tucson metro area. The first rescue occurred around 830 am LST on Silverbell Rd between Ina Rd and El Camino del Cerro. Around the same time, flood waters 1 to 2 feet deep rushed across Sahuarita Rd near Calle Rinconado. A swift water rescue by the Corona de Tucson FD occurred around 10 am on South Houghton Rd near East Andrada Rd. A third rescue of a woman and her child occurred around 1120 am on South Desert Sunrise Trail near W Snyder Hill Rd. Both Andrada and Pantano High Schools were evacuated and closed early as a precaution due to road closures and a possible sinkhole. Classes resumed the next day.

Two homes on Camino del Rancho were flooded, displacing 9 people. The Red Cross provided temporary housing the the families. Numerous roads were closed around town. Over 1 inch of rain fell, and culverts were damaged along SR-80. Effects were exacerbated from heavy rain which also fell the previous day.

Nearly two inches of rain in parts of Nogales, Sonora caused Nogales Wash to overtop the Doe St. bridge in Nogales, Arizona.  As a result, businesses were flooded along Hohokam Drive with surface runoff 8 inches deep. Morley Avenue was also flooded.
Heavy rain caused Blanco Wash to flood Tucker Road west of Picture Rocks. Several inches of water also covered the road near Avra Valley Rd and Anway Rd.
Heavy rain of about 2.5 inches in 1 hour caused flash flooding south of Sierra Vista. Miller Creek overflowed Moson Rd while Ramsey Rd and Arabian Rd were also flooded.

Three to four inches or more of rainfall in one to two hours caused Sonoita Creek to overflow its banks into parts of Patagonia. Eight mobile homes were evacuated as a precaution with water 18 inches deep surrounding them. An additional 14 homes were also evacuated. Only minimal damage occurred to the skirting of these homes since they were elevated off the surface.
Heavy rain caused flooding across Park Link Drive over one foot deep in some spots. This caused some of the edges of the road to be washed out.

Heavy rain of 1.5 to 2.5 inches in 90 minutes caused widespread flash flooding in Tucson and resulted in a total of 45 stranded motorist calls and 8 swift water rescues. One rescue involved a Pima County Supervisor, who was swept away in her vehicle near Ft. Lowell and Oracle Rd. Flood waters caused major road damage near Lee St. and Santa Rosa Avenue. The Stone St. underpass was flooded to a depth of 8 feet. Flash flooding also caused delays and closures along Sandario Rd in Picture Rocks. Near Silverbell Rd and Speedway Rd, multiple lower level townhouses incurred flood damage. A few residences in Green Valley suffered minor flooding.

Three to four inches of rainfall in 1 to 2 upstream, Sonoita Creek overtopped the spillway at Patagonia Lake and flooded areas below the Lake downstream to Rio Rico. A portion of Pendelton Drive near Avenida Coatimundi in Rio Rico where Sonoita Creek crosses the road was barricaded during the day. At 2115 LST a motorist was stranded after he drove around the barricades and attempted to cross the water.
Heavy rain caused Peck Canyon to overflow its banks and flood adjacent streets in Rio Rico.

Heavy rain caused ponding of water along Highway 79 north of Park Link Drive, and caused Durham Wash and other small washes to flow across the highway, making it impassable for 2 hours. Farther south, heavy rain also occurred near I-10 along the Pinal/Pima county line. Flash flooding occurred at Pinal Air Park, where flood waters entered several buildings. Runoff flooded small washes near Red Rock and washed out Sasco Road at the Santa Cruz River.

Heavy rain upstream from Tucson and along smaller washes near Ironwood National Monument caused strong flows in the Santa Cruz River, which breached a dirt barrier near Sunland Gin Road south of Arizona City. The water reached four feet at its maximum depth. The roadway was closed for nearly two days which cutoff the only access for residents of Silverbell Estates to the southwest.

Several inches of rainfall caused significant flows on the McClellan and Durham Washes. Water traveled downstream, overflowing at in spots into parts of Picacho and Eloy. This caused flooding and a few evacuations of homes east of I-10. Significantly impacted areas included Picacho Blvd at Oak Lane, Picacho Hwy at Camino Adelante, and Houser Rd at SR-87.

A swift water rescue occurred on South Burro Drive south of Ramsey Road in Hereford. Two people and their dog were rescued when their vehicle was washed down a low water crossing. No injuries occurred. Additionally, a portion of Leonardo de Vinci Drive in Sierra Vista was closed due to flash flooding.

Hail up to 1 inch in diameter occurred for a time near along Kolb Road near Escalante Rd, 29th St, and Golf Links Rd. One home near Kolb Rd and 29th St sustained damage when hail broke 5 double-paned skylights.
Golfball size hail was reported in Oracle.

A large tree fell on a mobile home near Flowing Wells Rd and Wetmore Road causing damage. The tree was dead and had little root system. An 81-yr old woman and her cat were rescued by fire fighters but were uninjured.
Thunderstorms produced brief heavy rain that caused 6 to 12 inches of water to flow over Dragoon Road and Old Ranch Road.
Sustained easterly winds at 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph caused multiple power poles to be bent down along Madera Canyon Road. At least one will need to be replaced.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a tree near Golf Links Rd and Prudence Rd.

One inch diameter hail began around 2300 LST as a large thunderstorm moved through Safford. The storm eventually produced hail up to 2.5 inches in diameter. Homes, vehicles and property were damaged throughout Safford and Solomon. Copious amounts of smaller hail fell for 20 minutes in some locations, causing accumulations of up to 6. In many spots, the hail did not melt overnight and was still piled up on roads, sidewalks and yards the following morning. In addition, where hail broke windows, rain and additional hail entered buildings causing water damage. This caused some schools in Safford to remain closed for two weeks until repairs were completed. The hailstorm also wiped out around 4000 acres of cotton crop, with several million dollars of loss estimated. Graham County issued a disaster declaration in the wake of the storm.

More than two inches of rain accompanied by large hail that piled up to six inches deep in some locations caused flash flooding in Safford.  Runoff filled Freeman Wash which caused minor damage to several homes and a school, and washed out part of 12th Avenue. The flood waters temporarily displaced twenty five residents. The school was closed for two weeks until repairs were completed. Flood waters also blocked roadways in rural areas, stranding 8,000 county fair visitors until waters receded.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: Heavy snow occurred in the higher elevations of Graham and Greenlee Coutnies along with strong winds. The Hannagan Meadow SNOTEL received about 18 inches of snow.
The higher elevations of the Galiuro and Pianelo mountains received heavy snow and strong winds. Estimates on Mt. Graham are of snow amounts around 2 feet.

Very heavy snow and strong damaging winds occurred on the Santa Catalina and Rincon Mountains. Numerous trees were toppled over along Catalina Highway near Mt. Lemmon. Additionally, one felled tree damaged a cable line on one of Ski Valley's ski lifts. Power was lost to most of the mountain for nearly 48 hours, and several communication and broadcast transmission towers were inoperable for several hours before backup generators functioned properly. Reports of 18 to 24 inches of snow were common. At lower elevations, rain caused rock slides that blocked portions of Catalina Highway and damaged guard rails.
Heavy snow and strong winds occurred on the higher elevations of the Chiricahua Mountains.
Heavy snow and strong winds occurred on the higher elevations of the Huachuca and Santa Rita mountains.
Heavy snow and strong winds occurred on the higher elevations of the Baboquivari Mountains including Kitt Peak.

Wind damage due to strong winds occurred in the Tucson Metro area. Tree damage constituted the majority of the wind damage, including substantial tree damage at Agua Caliente Park. Additionally, a power pole was blown down in Marana.
A recorded gust to 67 MPH occurred at Muleshoe Ranch in Cochise County. A small shed was blown over in Sierra Vista.
Large hail damaged several cars and residences in the community of Pima.
Thunderstorm winds damaged large tree limbs and a number of roofs in the community of Pima.

Two to three inches of rain caused Union Canal to overflow into the streets of Pima. In addition, flood damage occurred to cotton that was already harvested and being stored as modules in area fields.
Strong winds peeled off a considerable portion of the metal roof of a house in Willcox.

events.cz_name: UPPER GILA RIVER AND ARAVAIPA VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: A recorded wind gust to 59 MPH from the northwest occurred at the Safford airport at 6:57 pm MST as a cold front passed.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: The higher elevations of Graham and Northern Greenlee County received in excess of 12 of snow based on area reports.
The higher elevations of the Pinaleno Mountains including Mt. Graham received in excess of 12 of snow.
The higher elevations of the Huachuca and Santa Rita Mountains received in excess of 12 of snow.
The higher elevations of Mt. Lemmon received about 12-18 of snow.

Strong southwest winds lifted a tin roof off John's Apartments in Douglas. The roof contacted live electrical wires, which caused a power outage for more than a thousand customers.  The tin roof also caused damage to a nearby house. Six families in the apartment complex needed to find alternate housing for the night.
Sabino Creek rose above 6 feet as heavy rainfall upstream on the Catalina Mountains caused long duration runoff into the Valley.
Localized amounts of rainfall in excess of 8 inches occurred on Mt. Lemmon causing extensive flooding and rock slides. Several people in Tucson needed to be rescued from flowing washes.
The Blue River crested 4.5 feet above Bankfull stage due to heavy rainfall.
A swift water rescue took place in the Tanque Verde wash near North Wentworth Road and East Speedway Blvd.
A swift water rescue occurred about 4 am at the Canada Del Oro Wash near West Overton Road and North La Cholla Blvd.
Snowfall in excess of 2 feet occurred in numerous areas on Highway 191 from Blue Vista to Hannagan Meadow.
Heavy snowfall occurred in northern parts of Graham County above 6000 feet.

Dust blowing across Interstate 10 reduced visibility near San Simon to near zero which resulted in three separate collisions involving a total of eight vehicles. Two minor injuries occurred. The interstate was closed for nearly four hours.
Interstate 10 near San Simon was closed for over four hours to very low visibility in blowing dust.
Interstate 10 was closed for over six hours near San Simon due to very low visibility in blowing dust.
Kitt Peak, at an elevation just below 7,000 feet had 7 inches of snowfall.
The town of Oracle at about 4500 feet had 3 inches of snowfall.

Numerous locations between 3000 feet and 5000 feet in the Tucson Metro area and Catalina Mountains had in excess of 2 inches of snowfall. Higher elevations across Southeast Arizona above 7000 feet had 7 to 15 inches of snow.
Hannagan Meadow recorded 15 inches of snowfall.
Numerous locations in Graham County below 5000 feet had in excess of 2 inches of snowfall. Higher elevations across Southeast Arizona above 7000 feet had 7 to 15 inches of snow.
Numerous locations below 5000 feet including the Canelo area and Highway 83 had in excess of 2 inches of snowfall.
Numerous locations in Cochise County including Texas Canyon, Mescal and the Kartchner Caverns had several inches of snowfall.
Interstate 10 near San Simon was closed for about three hours to very low visibility in blowing dust.

The human-caused Sawmill Fire started 10 miles southeast of Green Valley near Box Canyon and quickly spread east northeast for 20 miles across southeast Pima County and burned 28 percent of the Las Cienegas National Conservation Area. As it crossed State Route 83, two miles of guard rails and supporting posts were destroyed along with several power poles and road signs.  While no structures were damaged, about a hundred residents of rural communities such as Singing Valley were evacuated for a day or two, including nuns from the Santa Rita Abbey. The road was closed for 3 days because of the wildfire. The fire was 94 percent contained by the end of April after burning 46,991 acres. No additional acreage was burned before the fire was fully contained on May 4th.

As it crossed State Route 83, two miles of guard rails and supporting posts were destroyed along with several power poles and road signs. The road was closed for 3 days because of the wildfire. The fire was 94 percent contained by the end of April after burning 46,991 acres. No additional acreage was burned before the fire was fully contained on May 4th.
Interstate 10 near San Simon was closed for about four hours due to very low visibility in blowing dust.
Interstate 10 near San Simon was closed for about seven hours due to very low visibility in blowing dust.

The human caused Mulberry Fire started on May 6th, eight miles southeast of Vail, east of State Route 83 in the Empire Mountains.  The wildfire destroyed four structures including two homes as it spread rapidly northeast.  A total of twenty rural residences were evacuated.  The wildfire consumed 1755 acres before being contained on May 9th.

Lightning started a vacant structure on fire in Dragoon Estates.  The building was totally destroyed and the fire spread into adjacent grass and brush, scorching 120 acres.  Twelve nearby residents were evacuated before the fire was contained the next day. At least two other brush fires were ignited by lightning during the afternoon, from just east of the Whetstone Mountains to east of Tombstone along Davis Road.
A dust devil damaged a storage shed on the northeast edge of Saint David. A sheet-metal roof extension was detached from the main structure and thrown about 50 yards.
A dust devil peeled the composite roofing material off the flat-topped roof of a home near 22nd and Wilmot in Tucson.  Cracks in the roof/ceiling of the house also resulted.
Between 1 and 1.5 inches of rain on the Burro Fire burn scar caused flash flooding near Rose Canyon and Scout Ranch.
A severe wind gust was measured at Nogales Airport.
A severe wind gust was measured at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base. Two trees were snapped near the intersection of Lisa Frank and Universal Way.
Thunderstorm winds blew roofs off a couple houses and collapsed another. Winds also knocked down several power lines. Sells RAWS measured a gust of 62 mph.
Heavy rain caused a rollover accident on Interstate 19 just south of the Duval Mine Road exit. No injuries were reported.
Lightning struck a tree in Green Valley and caught it on fire.

Temperatures topped out between 108 and 111 degrees in parts of the Tucson Metro area on June 6th and 7th.  The highest temperature recorded at the Tucson International Airport during this period was 107 degrees on the 7th.
An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperatures during the period were 118 at Ajo and 117 at Organ Pipe National Monument.
An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperatures during the period was 115 degrees at Sells.

events.cz_name: UPPER SANTA CRUZ RIVER AND ALTAR VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperatures during the period were 112 degrees at Sasabe and Nogales Airport.

An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The Tucson International Airport reached 115 degrees on three consecutive days for the first time ever and recorded the 2nd warmest reading on record of 116 degrees on the 20th.  The low temperature of 87 on the 20th was the warmest on record for June. Dozens of heat-related illnesses were reported in the Tucson Metro, but no fatalities were reported.
An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperature recorded during the period was 115 degrees at Picacho Peak.
An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperature recorded during the period was 111 degrees at San Manuel.

An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperatures recorded during the period were 115 at Cascabel, 112 at Benson and 110 at Sierra Vista and Tombstone.

events.event_narrative: An extended period of excessive heat occurred across nearly all of southeast Arizona. The highest temperature recorded during the period were 113 at the Safford Ag Center, 112 at the Safford Airport and 110 at Duncan.

Lightning sparked the Frye Fire on June 7th. The fire began to spread rapidly on June 19th as the result of strong winds from a thunderstorm outflow boundary. On that day, the Webb Peak Lookout Tower was damaged and the water chlorination shed at Old Columbine was destroyed. The observatory on Mount Graham was threatened but spared from the wildfire through suppression. By the end of June, the fire had consumed 42,755 acres but was only 45% contained.
The lightning caused Frye Fire ignited on June 7th. About 6,000 of the total 48,443 acres were burned during July before the fire was fully contained on July 20th.

The Burro Fire started in the foothills of the southeast side of the Santa Catalina Mountains northwest of Redington Pass.  The fire was less than a 1,000 acres in size at the end of June but grew considerably during July.

The Burro Fire started in the foothills of the southeast side of the Santa Catalina Mountains on June 30th, then quickly spread both northwest and southeast during July.  Summerhaven and other residences on the mountain were evacuated for several days.  Mt. Lemmon Highway and Redington Pass Road were both closed to traffic. The number of acres burned totaled 27,238 but no structures were lost.

The Burro Fire started in the foothills of the southeast side of the Santa Catalina Mountains on June 30th, then quickly spread both northwest and southeast during July.  Summerhaven and other residences on the mountain were evacuated for several days.  Mt. Lemmon Highway and Redington Pass Road were both closed to traffic. The number of acres burned totaled 27,238 but no structures were lost.
Thunderstorm winds broke off a 4 inch diameter tree limb near Patagonia Lake.

The lightning caused Bowie Fire started on June 7th on the northwest side of the Chiricahua Mountains near Fort Bowie and was spread by gusty winds. The Fort Bowie National Historic Site was closed due to the fire and the Diamond Mountain Retreat Center was evacuated. A total of 3,036 acres burned.

The lightning caused Bowie Fire started on June 7th on the northwest side of the Chiricahua Mountains near Fort Bowie and was spread by gusty winds. The Fort Bowie National Historic Site was closed due to the fire and the Diamond Mountain Retreat Center was evacuated. A total of 3,036 acres burned.
Thunderstorm outflow winds blew across southeast Cochise County. The strongest wind gusts was 63 mph, which was recorded at the KDUG ASOS. Power lines were downed near McNeal.

The lightning caused Encino Fire ignited on June 20th south of Sonoita and spread rapidly north due to thunderstorm outflow winds. At least five homes and 30 power poles were destroyed by the fire. Many residents of Sonoita were evacuated and State Routes 82 and 83 were both closed temporarily. A firefighter was injured when he broke his ankle. The fire was fully contained by June 25th after burning 1289 acres.
Thunderstorm winds caused roof damage to one building south of Sierra Vista.
Sybil Road at Dragoon Wash was impassable due to flash flooding.
Thunderstorm outflow winds blew across northern Santa Cruz Count. The Hopkins RAWS measured a 58 mph gust.
Thunderstorm winds downed 3 trees in various locations in Green Valley.
Thunderstorm wind gust of 64 mph recorded at a state-owned agricultural weather station near Safford. A large tree was downed along Highway 70 in Solomon.
Landspout tornado occurred in the vicinity of Sandario and Barnett Roads. Tornado remained over open desert with no damage noted.

The lightning caused Lizard Fire started in the Dragoon Mountains on June 7th and quickly spread due to strong winds. The fire merged with the Dragoon Fire which caused an increase in acreage to nearly 15,000 acres. The communities of Dragoon and Cochise Stronghold were evacuated. One home and two outbuildings were destroyed in Dragoon.  The fire continued into July before it was fully contained but the overall acreage did not grow much beyond 15,000 acres.

The fire merged with the Dragoon Fire which caused an increase in acreage to nearly 15,000 acres. The communities of Dragoon and Cochise Stronghold were evacuated. One home and two outbuildings were destroyed in Dragoon.  The fire continued into July before it was fully contained but the overall acreage did not grow much beyond 15,000 acres.

The lightning caused Lizard Fire started in the Dragoon Mountains on June 7th and quickly spread due to strong winds. The fire merged with the Dragoon Fire which caused an increase in acreage to nearly 15,000 acres. The fire was not fully contained until July 19th but additional fire spread was minimal during July with a total of 15,230 acres consumed.

A thunderstorms wind gusts of 66 MPH was recorded at the KDUG ASOS.

The Swisshelms Fire started on June 27th in the Swisshelms Mountains and spread quickly due to strong winds. By the end of June the fire had consumed 7250 acres.  The fire was not fully contained until July 10th after a total of 10,950 acres burned.

Thunderstorm winds caused roof damage to a house near S. Broken Spur Lane and W. Illinois Street and downed several large trees and damaged roofs and carports in Copper Crest.
Thunderstorm produced a gust of 58 mph at Safford Airport. Outflow winds continued toward the northwest to the north of Safford.
Ephriam Wash overflowed its banks at Western Avenue bridge. Nearby rain gauge recorded 2.17 inches of rain in about an hour.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding of the Camino de Oeste Wash. This caused Silverbell Road to be closed between Sweetwater and Goret roads. Swift water rescue occurred where Camino de Oeste Wash crossed Lloyd Bush Drive. Stone Avenue underpass south of 6th Street flooded 7 feet deep.
Marana ASOS measured a wind gust of 58 mph and a tree was down in the eastbound lane at I-10 and Tangerine Road.
Flash flooding caused Hawser Street between Twin Lakes Drive and Coronado Forest Drive in Catalina to close.
Flash flooding caused Twin Peaks Road at Sanders Road to be closed.
Stone Street underpass was closed due to flash flooding to a depth of 8 feet.

Flash flooding caused Moore Road to be closed between Sanders Road and the I-10 frontage road as well as Tangerine Road at I-10. Another area of flash flooding caused Snyder Hill Road to be closed between Desert Sunrise and Sandario roads in southwest Tucson.
Heavy rains fell across the Frye Fire burn scar and caused flash flooding in Ash Creek. An 8 pipeline leading to Cluff Pond 3 was washed away and several private outbuildings were damaged.

A strong thunderstorm moved through the Tucson metro area during the afternoon with many reports of damage in central and western Tucson. The highest measured wind speed was 49 mph near 7th Street and Campbell. Large trees were uprooted along Kino Parkway and Silverlake Road, near Park and 20th Street, near Stone and 6th Street, near Echols Avenue and 5th Street, and near the McKale Center on the University of Arizona campus. The tree that fell on the U of A campus fell on two parked cars. There was also a power pole down at Speedway Boulevard and I-10.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree near Park Place Mall, blocking part of Broadway Blvd. Winds also peeled off most of the roof from a residence near 22nd and Wilmot.

Heavy rain caused two homes were flooded on West and Oak Street, but no injuries were reported. Heavy rain in Nogales, Sonora caused Nogales wash to overflow its banks whch caused road closures at Doe Street, Calle Sonora, Hohokam Street and at the Baffert Drive Bridge. Damage to the Nogales Wash caused by the strong flows, and subsequently the International Outfall Interceptor, were discovered days later. Raw sewage from this line flowed into the wash.  This ultimately led to a month long effort by local, state and federal officials to repair the wash and interceptor pipe. The flow was diverted to avoid contaminating water farther downstream, but some contamination of local groundwater likely occurred. The total repair project including labor, fuel, equipment and other resources totaled nearly $5 million.
Heavy rain caused water nearly a foot deep to flow across West Chula Vista Rd as well as near Orange Grove and 1st Avenue.
Five inch diameter mesquite tree snapped in half off Duval Mine Road 5 miles west of Green Valley.
Sabino Creek at Sabino Dam spiked to 2.68 feet in 30 minutes. Twenty six hikers were trapped and had to be rescued due to flood waters over the bridge.

Flash flooding in Ash Canyon from Frye Fire burn scar damaged at least two homes, a chicken barn and an RV, and closed Cluff Ranch Road in several locations. An undisclosed number of people were stranded in the Cluff Pond recreation area and had to be rescued. Damage also occurred to Route 366 near Ladybug Saddle and Wet Canyon from flash flooding off the same burn scar.

Heavy rain on the Rincon Mountains caused high flows on Tanque Verde Creek and Rincon Creek. Redington Pass Road was flooded and Rincon Creek at Rincon Gauge recorded a crest of 9.32 feet. This is the fourth highest on record for this site.
A brief landspout tornado occurred over open country south of Saint David.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree near Broadway Boulevard and Houghton Road.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a tree on Ajo Road near Kino Stadium.
Flash flooding caused a vehicle to be swept away on Cascabel Road. Driver was swept three-quarters of a mile downstream to the San Pedro River resulting in the need to be rescued.

Heavy rain over the Fry Fire burn scar and south of Safford caused Marijilda and Swift Canyons to overflow their banks. A vehicle was swept off of W Concho Street, trapping the driver until rescuers arrived.  A second vehicle was completely submerged on Stockton Road. Three teenagers were able to escape from the vehicle.
Heavy rain falling on the Frye Fire Burn scar caused flooding of the Wet Canyon Campground/Picnic Area.
A border patrol SUV parked near the international border and the Santa Cruz River became stuck in the mud and became overrun by the floodwaters of the Santa Cruz River.

Flash flooding occurred on the northwest side of Tucson, north of West Ina Rd between Silverbell Road and I-10. Flash flooding also caused River Road to become impassable between Alvernon and Swan Roads.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding near Oracle and Drachman.
A mesquite tree was blown down near Pima and Beverly Streets.
The Safford ASOS (KSAD) reported a wind gust of 67mph.
Flash flooding occurred along a portion of Sands Ranch Road in Whetstone causing the road to be temporarily shut down.

Heavy rain caused widespread flash flooding in southwest Tucson. Mission Road at Valencia was impassable. Camino de la Tierra and Valencia was also closed, and portions of Camino De Oeste Road were closed. Several vehicles became stranded in the flood waters.
Flash flooding caused Silverbell Road near Sweetwater Drive to become impassable.
Near Solomon, AZ the San Jose Canal overflowed its banks.
Heavy rain over the Frye Fire burn scar caused a wall of water down Ash Creek that uprooted 18-inch diameter trees and rushed across Cluff Ranch Road. Also, the Wet Canyon channel topped Route 366.

Heavy rain caused Rock Creek and Turkey Creek to overflow their banks and caused road closures of Turkey Creek Road, Cross Creek Road and State Route 181.  Some yards were flooded and some residents were cut off for several days due to washed out roads.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Tucson. One car became submerged in flowing water a foot deep near Country Club and Bantam roads.

The Roach Fire quickly spread down the San Pedro River bed near Dudleyville due to strong winds in the channel.  One home, four unoccupied residences, and nine other structures were destroyed.  About 100 residents were briefly evacuated. Highway 77 was also closed for a short time the night the fire started. The fire burned 335 acres before it was contained. One firefighter suffered a heat-related injury.
Three people were trapped at Tanque Verde Falls and unable to cross the wash to exit the area due to a rapid increase in water levels.

Heavy rain caused water several feet deep across several roadways in rural Marana including Twin Peaks Road between Sandario and Sanders Roads, Avra Valley Road at the Brawley Wash and portions of Clayton Road.
Tree were uprooted on 14th Ave between Glenn Street and Kelso Street. Also, a large tree fell on house on Glenn Street between Fairview Ave and 15th Ave.

Over one hundred eucalyptus and other large shallow-rooted trees were toppled and many other tree limbs were downed on the east side of Tucson. The damage path from this severe thunderstorm was about a mile and a half either side of a line from Broadway Blvd. and Kolb Road to Tanque Verde and Sabino Canyon Roads.  Several trees fell on to buildings near Speedway Blvd. and Pantano Road, including the Woodridge Apartment complex, which sustained significant damage to several units.  One of the trees also crushed an automobile. Many other trees damaged retaining walls or power lines when they were downed. At least one power pole was also snapped. At least 7,000 customers were without power for several hours. Additionally, the roof was ripped off one house near 5th St. and Kent Drive.

An excavator became buried in about four feet of mud after the Nogales Wash flooded. Was buried up to the operator's cabin and had to be pulled out via tow truck. Additionally, a stream gauge in the Nogales Wash recorded a level of 10.4 feet at 3pm, which is almost 2.5 feet above flood level.

A swift water rescue was conducted along Ina Road near Camino de los Caballos when a car was swept 20 feet off the road due to flash flooding.  Sandario Road also became inundated by flood waters between Avra Valley and Twin Peaks Roads.
Several trees were downed across the town of Sahuarita.

Heavy rain inundated roads in the western portions of the Tucson Metro Area north and northeast of Ryan Field.  A child was swept off her feet and was carried 20 yards downstream after attempting to cross a flooded roadway with water 3 to 4 feet deep.  She was found unconscious, but recovered.
Lightning started a house on fire in the 1000 block of Stronghold Canyon Lane in Sahuarita.
Portions of Anway Road were closed due to flash flooding in Avra Valley.
Power lines were downed by thunderstorm winds between First Ave. and Oracle Rd.
A short-lived funnel cloud was observed near the Arizona Motorplex on Los Reales Rd.
RAWS site in Sells measured a thunderstorm wind gust of 60mph.
Thunderstorms winds downed two power poles just south of Duncan. Power was lost in Duncan for several hours as a result.
Twenty three inches of snowfall occurred at Hannagan Meadow.
Six inches of snowfall occurred just below 5000 feet in elevation at Fort Grant.
The Benson area at an elevation below 4000 feet had 2-3 inches of snowfall. The Dragoon mountains also had about 3 inches of snow.
The town of Oracle had 4 inches of snow.
Rio Rico and Nogales, at an elevation below 4000 feet had about 2 inches of snow. In addition, Madera Canyon at about 5000 feet had 6 to 7 inches of snow.
Strong northeast winds downed several small trees at the residence of the Pinal County Emergency Manager.

The extreme drought (D3) category was reached in late January across southeast Pima County, Santa Cruz County and far southwest Cochise County including portions of the Tohono O'odham Nation and the Baboquivari, Santa Rita and Huachuca Mountains. The extreme drought category was also reached across the White Mountains of far northern Graham and Greenlee Counties.  Below normal precipitation occurred each month from August of 2017 through January of 2018.  Soil moisture readings were well below normal and ranked below the 20th percentile.

The human caused Adobe Fire started on April 2nd in southeast Cochise County and quickly spread through 261 acres of grass and dry brush by southwest winds gusting to between 30 and 35 mph. Ten residents were evacuated and several roads were closed after the onset of the fire due to the threat to nearby structures.  A small shed and a larger barn were lost as the fire jumped Double Adobe Road, but no injuries occurred.  The fire was largely contained after dark that evening, but was not fully contained until April 4th.

events.cz_name: WHITE MOUNTAINS OF GRAHAM AND GREENLEE COUNTIES
events.event_narrative: The Rattlesnake Fire started in Apache County on April 11th, then spread southeast into northeast Graham and northwest Greenlee Counties on April 13th due to strong northwest winds. The fire continued to spread southeast, mainly in Greenlee County, such that by the end of the month it had consumed about 26,000 acres.

Extreme drought (D3 category), which began in January, continued throughout February across the same sections of southeast Pima County, Santa Cruz County and far southwest Cochise County including portions of the Tohono O'odham Nation and the Baboquivari, Santa Rita and Huachuca Mountains, as well as the White Mountains of far northern Graham and Greenlee Counties.||While most of the area received between 2 and 4 inches of precipitation from one storm system in mid February, overall soil moisture readings only improved slightly, and generally remained ranked below the 20th percentile. Prior to the precipitation event, two human-caused wildfires burned in rural areas. The Altar Fire burned northwest of Sasabe, on Mildred Peak, and consumed 3400 acres. The Knob Hill Fire burned 2900 acres just outside of the extreme drought area near Saint David.

Heavy rainfall led to a vehicle accident on Interstate 19 near Rio Rico causing a fatality (indirect).

Extreme drought (D3 category), which began in January, continued throughout March across the same sections of southeast Pima County, Santa Cruz County and far southwest Cochise County including portions of the Tohono O'odham Nation and the Baboquivari, Santa Rita and Huachuca Mountains, but expanded westward from the White Mountains in northern Graham and Greenlee Counties across the San Carlos Apache Tribe lands of northwestern Graham County.||While some rain did fall in the extreme drought area, amounts were light, ranging from 10 to 50 percent of normal for March in northern areas and less than 25 percent of normal in southern areas. Overall soil moisture readings generally remained ranked below the 20th percentile, but wildfire activity was suppressed as a result of the widespread precipitation event that occurred in mid February. Levels in the San Carlos Reservoir, which had been hovering between 7 and 8 percent of capacity through the winter, dropped to near 6 percent by the end of March.
Minor wind damage occurred at the site of a commercial building that was under construction in Sierra Vista. Several of the metal studs were bent and dislodged from the slab.

Lightning ignited the Bruno Fire just east of Leslie Canyon Wildlife Refuge on July 24. The fire spread into the Pedrogosa Mountains and burned 3038 acres on state lands and 1409 acres of the Coronado National Forest for a total of 4447 acres before becoming contained on July 31.

Thunderstorms created a wall of dust that traveled over 30 miles in southeast Pinal County, from Marana to Eloy, and beyond.  Visibility was reduced to less than a 1/4 mile with some reports of visibility down to zero at times, forcing the closure of Interstate 10 from Picacho Peak to Casa Grande.

Thunderstorm winds blew down a large aluminum light fixture over on Kino Parkway and 22nd St, temporarily closing the road to southbound traffic. About two miles away, winds also blew down a dead tree, which damaged the roof of a house.
Thunderstorm winds damaged an RV southeast of Why and the roof of a home in Gunsight Village.
Trees were downed by thunderstorm winds at 1st and Oracle as well as near Overton Road and Shannon Road in Oro Valley.
A gustnado caused damage to the awning and patio roof in Three Points.
Over two inches of rain caused flowing water up to a foot deep across several roads in Oro Valley.
Lightning damaged computer, communications, and radio equipment at the Oro Valley Police Department.
A power pole was downed by thunderstorm winds about 10 miles northeast of Sells.
Seven power poles were downed by thunderstorm winds 12 miles southwest of Chuichu.
Thunderstorm winds blew a tree down near Cortaro Farms and Magee Roads.

Thunderstorms produced 2 to 3 inches of rain in around on hour on both sides of I-10 from Cortaro to Twin Peaks which caused flash flooding.  Some of these areas had als received 1 to 2 inches of rain two days earlier. Many roads and intersections were closed due to flash flooding on the northwest side of Tucson encompassing an area from Tangerine Rd and I-10 down to Ina Rd and I-10. First responders performed at least eight swift water rescues of motorists. A restaurant and animal shelter were also flooded, along with damage to Sanctuary Cove foot trail.  A total of 8 swift water rescues had to be performed. Flood waters damaged railroad tracks and derailed over two dozen Union Pacific railroad cars north of Twin Peaks Road, causing extensive damage and closing the access road to Interstate 10 for several days.

Excessively hot temperatures of 105 to 113 degrees were observed below 5000 feet in southeast Arizona.  High temperature records at the Tucson International Airport were tied on July 23 with 109 degrees and broken on the 24th and 25th with highs of 112 and 110 degrees, respectively. On July 23rd, the Safford Airport reached 112 degrees and San Simon topped out at 108. A temperature of 111 degrees was attained at Sells on July 25th and at Ajo and at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument on both the 24th and 25th. Benson reached 110 on all three days.  Record highs were set at Bisbee-Douglas Airport on the 23rd and 24th with 105 and 104 degrees, respectively.  Tucson Fire responded to at least six heat-related calls on July 24th. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for two adult males. One occurred just east of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument on the 24th. The second occurred on the Tohono O'odham Nation near the International Border.  The exact time of death was not determinable, but very likely occurred on July 25th.

High temperatures from July 5th through July 7th were between 105 and 113 from Tucson westward across Pima County and in southwest Pinal County, which were significantly above normal. Respective high temperatures include: Tucson International Airport 111 (record), 105 and 107 degrees; Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument 113, 113 (record) and 109 degrees; Sells 113 (record), 107 and 106 degrees; and Picacho 111, 109, 110 degrees.  Green Valley also set a record high temperature of 108 degrees on July 7th. A hiker suffering from heat exhaustion at Sabino Canyon was rescued and taken to a hospital for treatment on July 8th. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for two adult males, one on the grounds of Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument on the 5th and another on the Tohono O'odham Nation south of Sells near the International Border on the 7th.

High temperatures between 108 and 113 were common from Tucson westward across Pima County and in southwest Pinal County. A record high temperature of 111 degrees was tied at the Tucson International Airport. Sells reached 113 degrees and Ajo topped out at 109 degrees.

Heavy rain led to flash flooding on the Frye fire burn scar. The Route 366 road surface and a culvert were damaged due to flooding of Grant Creek.
One to two inches of rain over the Frye Fire burn scar resulted in flash flooding and damage to Route 366 near Hospital Flat Campground.
Hail as large as 1.5 inches in diameter fell near Corona De Tucson, damaging a number of vehicles.
Thunderstorm winds knocked down seven power poles along Dragoon Rd forcing it to close for a several hours.

Thunderstorm winds damaged a house near Freeman Street and Broadway Boulevard. The family was displaced as the home was deemed unlivable at that time due to the damages. Other houses sustained roof damage and several nearby trees and cacti were also blown down. Outflow winds also downed a tree in the Target parking lot at 22nd St. and Old Spanish Trail.

A mobile home with a resident inside on Morin Road was overturned and heavily damaged due to a thunderstorm wind gust. Three trees were also downed near milepost 3 of Frontier Road, and power lines were knocked down near Frontier Road and Double Adobe Road.  The ASOS at the Bisbee-Douglas Airport recorded a wind gust to 58 mph at 1828 MST.
Thunderstorm winds blew down power poles north of North Komelik resulting in power outages in neighboring communities that lasted until the following morning.
Flash flooding caused off ramps along I-10 in the Eloy and Picacho areas to become impassable.
A driver lost control of her vehicle on I-10 east of Benson due to heavy rain and wet roads and hydroplaned into a palo verde tree.
Heavy rain and wet roads resulted in a car hydroplaning and veering off Interstate 10 near San Simon.  The car sustained minimal damage but the motorist was uninjured.
Thunderstorm winds blew down fences and damaged a few trees in San Manuel.

One to two inches of heavy rain in less than one hour collapsed the roof of a dentist's office in Kearny, flooding the office. The heavy rain also allowed 50 mph wind gusts to down a large dead tree.  No other damage resulted.
Thunderstorm winds downed power lines near Irvington and Houghton Roads, which resulted in over 2,500 customers losing power for two hours.
Heavy rain caused a motorcycle accident on Mt. Lemmon Highway near mile post 4.

Brief heavy rain from a thunderstorm resulted a single vehicle crash on Interstate 19 in Green Valley. After the driver lost control of the vehicle, it crashed into a tree in the median. All three occupants were taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries.

One to three inches of rain destabilized the soil that compromised the town of Mammoth's water system by creating fractures in the water system lines. This caused the system to be shut down and the town to declare a state of emergency.

Extreme drought (D3 category) continued through early August across western Pima and south central Pinal counties including the Tohono O'odham Nation. Rainfall amounts for the month ranged from 0.50 to 3 inches. This was sufficient to raise soil moisture levels above the 20th percentile for the first time since 2017 and cause these areas to be upgraded to the severe drought (D2 category) by the middle of the month.

Rescues of 23 hikers suffering from heat exhaustion occurred in the foothills of the Santa Catalina Mountains.

Several mobile home sustained patio and/or roof damage near I-10 and Kolb and a tree was downed in Sycamore Park as a result of thunderstorm winds. The Tucson ASOS reported a 60 mph wind gust at 713 pm.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees south of Skyline Drive between 1st Ave and Campbell Ave.
Thunderstorm winds blew down two power poles along Indian Route 15 near Ak Chin village.
San Simon ADOT weather station measured a wind gust of 61 mph.
Large tree was downed near the intersection of Rancho Sahuarita and Pima Mine Road. A gazebo was also damaged.
Water 8-12 inches deep was running across Sahuarita Road near Kolb Road.
Old Nogales Highway at Summit Street closed due to flash flooding.
Five power poles were downed near Cockelbur and Viava Vo Farms.
Hail one inch in diameter was reported near Catalina at 345 pm with golf ball size hail reported near Catalina State Park at 400 pm.
Thunderstorm winds destroyed solar panels which were on the room of a home in Oro Valley near Tangerine Road and 1st Avenue.
Flash flooding from heavy rain caused Kino Springs Blvd to become impassable near Kino Springs Gold Course.

One to two inches of rain fell on the west side of the Tucson Metro area between 1 and 3 am.  This led to flooding and the subsequent closure of several roads in Picture Rocks, including Clayton Road between Twin Peaks and Avra Valley Roads and Scrub Brush Road near Trico Road. One woman was rescued from a car in 4 feet of water on Manville Road at the Brawley Wash.

Two to three inches of rain caused flash flooding and road closures within Catalina State Park.  While roads were not damaged, many became covered with mud and debris.  The park remained closed until the afternoon of the following day.
Lightning struck a house near Sunrise and Kolb. The chimney was struck by lightning which caused an eight-foot split down the brick. No other damage was noted.

Up to 1.5 inches of rain in less than 1 hour caused rapid flows on Flato Wash which swept away a vehicle on Old Nogales Highway.  The lone driver, who had driven around police barricades, and the vehicle were swept downstream to the west side of main Nogales Highway where the vehicle rested on its top, but remained submerged in flood waters.  Rescuers were unable to reach the driver in time to save him.
Heavy rain caused water to flow 3 feet deep across Arivaca Road between mile markers 17 and 18 near Batamote Wash.
Thunderstorms winds downed power lines and bent several power poles in Solomon.

Thunderstorm winds downed a tree that fell on a house on 7th Street in Safford and downed a power pole in Thatcher. In Eden, a power line a downed tree pulled down a power line, which set a tree on fire.
Heavy rain of 1.5 to 2.5 inches caused Peterson Wash to overflow Safford Bryce Road, north of the Gila River in Safford.

Heavy rain of 1.5 to 2 inches fell over a two hour period over and just east of the 2017 Lizard Fire Burn Scar.  A motorist drown when his car became stuck in flood waters on Cochise Stronghold Road a mile south of Dragoon Road.
Heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches caused flash flooding of several roads in Saint David. Pederson at Busby was partially washed out and 1 foot of water flowed across S. Miller Lane near Barry Lane.
About 1.5 inches of rain fell between 330 pm and 500 pm causing flash flooding along the Ali Chuk Wash. This made Route 1 impassable for vehicles for about two hours.

Thunderstorm winds blew over a U.S. Postal Service semi-tractor trailer that was traveling westbound on Interstate 10 near San Simon.  The driver and passenger suffered minor injuries but were treated and released from a nearby hospital.  A nearby state DOT weather instrument measured a wind gust from the south of 83 mph at the time of the accident.
Thunderstorm winds downed three power poles near the Co-op Farms off Mission Road.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees on Pascua Yaqui tribal lands along and north of Hermans Road between Camino De Oeste and Victor Drive.
Heavy rain of around one inch in less than an hour flooded Mission Road and other roadways south of the San Xavier Mission.

Thunderstorm winds caused damage on Tucson's northwest side from about Ina and Shannon Roads westward to just east of I-10 and Cortaro Rd.  A power pole was downed on Camino De Oeste near Barque Dr. while numerous trees were downed elsewhere, some of which subsequently caused damage to cars, fences, retaining walls and parking structures.

Heavy rain of 1 to just over 2 inches in parts of Oro Valley, Tortolita and Casas Adobes caused flash flooding of several washes and significant street flooding.  At least four swift water rescues occurred at Camino De Oeste and Snow Leopard, Thornydale and Overton, Linda Vista and Highline, and Calle Maverick and Cerius Stravenue. Additionally, water flowed along Pima Farms Road up to the front porches of several homes.

Heavy rain of one to two inches on both sides of the International Border caused strong flows in Nogales Wash which severely damaged concrete slabs in the part of wash, and exposed the International Outfall Interceptor sewage line. Several streets in Nogales were also flooded with 1 to 2 feet of water.

Heavy rain of 1 to 1.5 inches caused flash flooding of Rodeo Wash on Tucson's south side. Two people were rescued from there SUV which was stuck in flood waters at South 16th Ave. and W. District St.  Two more vehicles were stuck in flood waters near Pennsylvania and Lundy.
A dust devil damaged several tents at a farmers market in Sierra Vista.  One person suffered a broken wrist and hand when a tent landed on her hand.

events.cz_name: UPPER GILA RIVER AND ARAVAIPA VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Extreme drought (D3 category) continued throughout September across far northern Graham County and a small portion of northwest Greenlee County including part of San Carlos Apache Tribal lands. Rainfall amounts ranged from 0.5 to 2 inches, which were 50 to 90 percent of normal for the month. While soil moisture levels increased, they remained below the 30th percentile. Levels in the San Carlos Reservoir rose by 5000 acre feet, but remained at less than 1 percent of capacity throughout September.

events.cz_name: UPPER GILA RIVER AND ARAVAIPA VALLEYS
events.event_narrative: Extreme drought (D3 category) was downgraded to severe drought (D2 category) by the middle of October across far northern Graham County and a small portion of northwest Greenlee County including part of San Carlos Apache Tribal lands. Rainfall amounts ranged from 2 to 4 inches, which were 125 to 250 percent of normal for the month, causing soil moisture levels to increase to above the 70th percentile. Levels in the San Carlos Reservoir rose by 5000 acre feet, but were still at less than 2 percent of capacity. However, this marked the first time since early June that the reservoir levels rose above 1 percent of capacity.

Thunderstorms produced 1 to 2 inches of rain over the Frye Fire burn scar early in the afternoon.  This caused flash flooding along the creeks on east side of the burn scar.

Thunderstorms produced periods of heavy rain totaling 2 to 3 inches during the early morning hours.  Interstate 10 near Bowie was closed in both directions due to flash flooding. Several swift water rescues were performed.

Thunderstorms produced 3 to 5 inches of rain along Sopori Wash and in Amado, which led to flash flooding in Amado.  Water flowed at depths ranging from 2 to 5 feet deep through several commercial properties including a restaurant, feed store, automotive shop, and youth center, causing substantial damage to the buildings and their contents.  Additionally, several RVs suffered water damage at a RV storage park. Minor damage also occurred to Arivaca Road and others in the area.

Thunderstorms produced localized heavy rain of 1 to 2 inches, causing flash flooding and erosion of road surfaces on Shannon Rd. north of Magee Rd. and near the intersection of Cortaro Farms Rd. and West Club Dr.
Tucker Rd at Blanca Wash was impassable with 3 feet of water running over the road.

During the late afternoon and evening 1.5-2.5 inches caused flash flooding in Thatcher. Two homes flooded and roads were flooded in Quail Ridge as the drainage canal overflowed. Farther north, several of the dorm rooms at the Eastern Arizona College|Campus, several of the Howards Place apartments on High School Avenue also suffered flood damage.

Heavy rain of 1 to 3 inches fell along and south of Sahuarita Road during the afternoon, causing washes to flow over Sahuarita Road up to two feet deep.  Several motorists were stranded in flood waters.

Widespread heavy rain of 2 to 4 inches with isolated amounts of 5 to 8 inches from 9 pm October 1st to 6 am October 2nd resulted in flash flooding, especially in the Gu Vo and Pisinemo Districts.  Indian Route 1 flooded between Pio Oik and Ali Chugk (Menagers) and homes were flooded in Ali Chugk.  Highway 86 was impassable between MP 80 and 90.  Indian Route 21 became flooded and impassable from just north of Pisinemo southward and flood waters topped the Vamori Wash bridge near Santa Cruz (Kom Vo).

Widespread heavy rain of 2 to 4 inches from 11 pm October 1st to 7 am October 2nd resulted in flash flooding, especially in the Gu Achi and Sif Oidak Districts. Indian Route 15 was flooded in spots from south of Santa Rosa to south of Chuichu and Indian Route 42 became flooded and impassable. Homes were flooded several villages including Anegam, San Luis and Kohatk.

Widespread heavy rain of 2 to 4 inches with isolated amounts of 5 to 8 inches fell mainly from the evening of October 1st through the morning hours of October 2nd. Runoff from this rainfall continued through the night of the 2nd, with the peak flows generally during the afternoon.  Several roads, including Indian Routes 1, 15, 21, 23, 34, and 45, as well as sections of Highway 86 became, or continued to be, impassable on the Tohono O'odham Nation. Several of these roads sustained significant damage.  Homes that were flooded earlier in the morning from flash flooding remained flooded or saw water levels rise.  Additional homes were flooded by continued runoff during the afternoon.  At least 50 homes were flooded in the following districts: Gu Vo (11); Pisinemo (17); Sif Oidak (20); and Hickiwan (2).  Several dozen residents were evacuated from their homes.  At least 20 earthen dams and levees were damaged along with the tribal water and utility system infrastructure. Runoff nearly filled Menagers Lake, prompting fears of a dam failure and the evacuation of the village of Ali Chugk.
Thunderstorm produced one inch diameter hail near Three Points and 1.5 diameter hail in Sahuarita.
Thunderstorm winds uprooted a tree at an apartment complex near La Canada Drive and Via Alamos Drive.

Heavy rain from widespread heavy showers and thunderstorms caused Highway 90 to be closed at Lobo Lane just north of Whetstone.  A one-vehicle rollover accident occurred near mile marker 304 due to water on the roadway prior to the highway's closure. No injuries were reported.

Heavy rain from thunderstorms caused several roads to be flooded in the Sahuarita area including sections of Wilmot Road and Nogales Highway.  One one car became stalled in flood waters on La Villita Road.
Nogales wash over-topped its banks. Flood waters dislodged and cracked three concrete panels that line the wash.

The human caused Babo Fire ignited southeast of Elgin during the morning of November 14th and quickly spread through grass by east wind gusts of 25 to 35 mph. The fire was contained on November 16th after it consumed 2473 acres.  Around 30 people were evacuated from the area at the fire's onset.

Heavy snow fell in the Catalinas with Summerhaven and Mount Lemmon Ski Valley reporting more than 15 inches of snow.  A semi-tractor trailer jackknifed in the snowy conditions on Mount Lemmon Highway, blocking both lanes of traffic.  The road closure resulted in about twenty people whose vehicles were farther up mountain having to spend the night in a shelter.
Bands of heavy snow impacted the higher elevations of the Pinaleno mountains with snowfall estimates on Mt. Graham of one foot or greater.

events.event_narrative: Accumulating snow began on the afternoon of December 31. By the morning of January 1 estimated snowfall totals in the White Mountains above 7000 feet were one foot or greater.
Accumulating snow began on the afternoon of December 31. By the morning of January 1 estimated snowfall totals in the Pinaleno Mountains above 7000 feet were one foot or greater.

events.event_narrative: Accumulating snow began on the afternoon of December 31. By the morning of January 1 estimated snowfall totals in the White Mountains above 7000 feet were one foot or greater.
