A severe wind gust was measured by a Pima County weather station located at the KEMX radar site.

Thunderstorm winds uprooted trees at Forty Niner Country Club and downed trees blocked roadways near the intersections of Old Spanish Trail and Houghton as well as Golf Links and Harrison. A wind gust of 79 mph was measured on Larkspur Rd.
Thunderstorm winds downed large branches along Woodland Rd. in northeast Tucson.
One to two inches of rain in less than 1 hour caused flash flooding of washes across roadways in northeast Tucson. One vehicle became stranded in floodwaters near Tanque Verde Rd and Conestoga Ave.

Another 1 to 2 of heavy rain in less than an hour with a 3-hour total of 2 to 4 caused additional flash flooding of washes and roadways on Tucson's northeast side. Three people were rescued when their vehicle was swept down Bonanza Wash near Bonanza Ave. and E Forest Grove Loop.
Two to four inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes up to 3 feet deep across Arivaca Rd. prompting its closure.
Two to four inches of rain in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes up to 3 feet deep across Arivaca Rd. prompting its closure.
Four power poles were downed along Dragoon Rd.
A downed tree fell on power lines along Sabin Rd. northwest of St. David.
One to two inches of rain fell in less than two hours east and southwest of Gleeson causing flash flooding across parts of Gleeson and Davis Rds.
One inch of rain in 30 minutes caused a rapid rise in Dragoon Wash and flash flooding across Sabin Rd. near St. David, making it impassable.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour southwest of Rio Rico caused roads in the area to become flooded and impassable.
Heavy rain of 1.5 in less than one hour near Kohatk resulted in minor flooding of two homes in that village.

Two to four inches of rain in less than two hours over the Bighorn burn scar area in the Santa Catalina Mountains caused flash flooding of several washes and roadways.  Sutherland Wash rose over 5 feet at a gauge just east of Oro Valley and the Canada del Oro Wash also rose, especially downstream of its confluence with the Sutherland Wash. Downstream flash flooding resulted at Overton Rd where 5 people were rescued from two different vehicles which were swept downstream.

Over one inch of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Sabino Canyon Recreation area and the closure of roadways. Several hikers were stranded and needed to be rescued after floodwaters rose.
Scout Camp RAWS measured a thunderstorm wind gust to 64 mph.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding across Davis Rd. between Tombstone and McNeal.

Heavy rain of 2 to 3 inches in less than an hour caused flash flooding of several roads in the Sierra Vista area including Moson Rd. and Nevada Rd. A fence near a residence was downed by a wall of water. The water line to the home was also damaged.
Two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding across Highway 86 near Indian Route 26 northwest of Sells.

A large area of two inches of rain occurred in three hours in east Tucson, generally east of Craycroft Rd. to the Rincon Mts. with more than 4 inches of rain from Broadway and Wilmot to Tanque Verde and Pantano Rds.  Numerous roads were flooded or damaged including Pima Rd. and Robb Wash. Several swift water rescues of motorists occurred including one vehicle washed downstream near Camino Loma Alta and Old Spanish Trail. Alamo Wash left its banks and flooded several homes between Pima and Speedway.
One inch of rain in less than 1 hour in Catalina Foothills caused flash flooding of River Rd. near Pontatoc Rd.
Two inches of rain caused the ceiling to collapse in an apartment complex near 22nd and Craycroft. Twelve apartments sustained damage.
Lightning struck a house on N Sweet Heather Way in Green Valley causing a small attic fire, which was quickly extinguished.
Heavy rain of 2 to 3.5 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding of washes and the closure of many roadways in Green Valley.
Heavy rain of 1 to 2 in 90 minutes caused flash flooding in rural areas west of Green Valley. Mission Rd. north of Duval Mine Rd. was closed.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour along Whitewater Draw caused flash flooding downstream where a vehicle abandoned in floodwaters was swept downstream at Kings Hwy. Brooks Rd. was also closed.

A broad area of 1.5 of rain, with pockets of 3 to 4, fell in less than 90 minutes and caused numerous road closures from Picture Rocks to Saguaro National Park West to southeast of Three Points. Kinney Rd. near Sonora Desert Museum was one of the major roads that was closed due to flooding.
One inch of rain in 30 minutes caused flash flooding of Highway 191 about 15 miles south of Safford.

One to three inches of rain in 2 hours caused flash flooding of roadways south and east of the Willcox Playa. One person was rescued from their vehicle after being stalled in flood waters on North Cochise Stronghold Rd.
Over an inch of rain in an hour caused flash flooding of roadways in Benson and State Route 80 in St. David. In Benson, one house and the community center were flooded.
The Hopkins RAWS measured a thunderstorm outflow gust to 68 mph.
A funnel cloud was photographed 10 miles north of Willcox.

More than 1 inch of rain in an hour caused flash flooding in northeast Tucson. Flash flooding was reported along Castle Rock Wash and one vehicle was stranded in flood waters near Bear Canyon and Tanque Verde Rds. Fort Lowell Rd. was closed due to flooding.

Two inches of rain in 1 to 2 hours caused flash flooding in central Cochise County.  Highway 191 near Birch Rd was flooded. Gleeson Rd. was washed out near mile post 20 and a swift water rescue occurred at mile post 14.
An inch of rain in 30 minutes caused flash flooding of Mescal Rd. Two occupants of a vehicle that drove into floodwaters were rescued 8 miles north of Mescal.
Two to three inches in one hour caused flash flooding of washes and several road closures in Oracle.
More than 1 inch of rain in less than an hour in the mountains north of State Rte. 266 caused flash flooding down the mountains and mud and rocks to block a portion of that route.

Two to four inches of rain in less than two hours caused flash flooding from east of Sierra Vista to north of Bisbee to Elfrida. Floodwaters deposited several rocks on State Rte. 80 near N. Old Divide Rd. northwest of Bisbee and caused the closure of Moson and Escapule Rds and the junction of State Rtes. 80 and 90 east of Sierra Vista. Along Davis Rd. near mile post 13, six motorists were rescued from three vehicles amidst floodwaters. Courtland and Jefferson Rds, northwest of Elfrida were also closed due to flooding.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding and road damage in,  as well as both north and east of Douglas. One person was rescued from their vehicle in floodwaters on Pedregosa Rd. near State Route 80. Leslie Canyon and Glen Rds. and Washington St. were closed due to flooding. Nine metal gates of the international border wall were damaged by Silver Creek flood waters just west of the San Bernardino National Wildlife Refuge.
Thunderstorm winds caused minor damage to four homes in Cockleburr and four homes in Anegam.
Lightning struck a water heater at one home starting a fire, and caused damage to an adjacent house near Sweetwater and Silverbell Dr. in west Tucson.
One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in Picture Rocks. Manville Rd. was closed due to flooding at the Brawley Wash and Sandario Rd. was also closed.

Two to three inches of rain in 2 hours along and south of Highway 86 caused flash flooding south of Ryan Field Airport and around Tucson Mountain Park Estates. Sierrita Mt. Rd. was closed near Hilltop Rd. and both Sandario Rd. and Snyder Hill Rd. was closed at the Black Wash.

One to two inches of rain in two hours caused flash flooding in Marana and Avra Valley. Anway Rd. was closed south of El Camino de Tres Arroyos as well as Silverbell Rd. near the Cocio Wash. Avra Valley Rd. was closed at the Brawley Wash.

Up to three inches of rain west and northwest of Tucson late in the evening caused flash flooding of Brawley Wash and smaller washes that flow into it.  An additional one to two inches of rainfall during the predawn hours south of Three Points flowed through the Altar Wash into the Brawley Wash causing flooding along it from northeast of Three Points through the Garcia Strip of the Tohono O'odham Nation, north to Marana from early that morning into late afternoon. Damage to area roads resulted.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in south central Pinal County. Considerable damage occurred to Park Links Rd. between Cattle Tank Rd. and the I-10 Frontage Rd. McClellan Wash also flooded Milligan Rd. resulting in its closure.

Flow in the Greene Wash resulting from 1 to 2 inches in southern Pinal County was enhanced by 2 to 4 inches of rain which fell during the early morning hours in northeast Pima County in the Brawley Wash and Santa Cruz River watersheds. The additional rainfall and runoff caused Greene Wash to flow 2 to 3 feet deep across Sunland Gin Rd for much of the afternoon causing damage to the road.

One inch of rain in 15 to 30 minutes created flash flooding of washes and roadways in a small portion of east Tucson. A vehicle was stranded in flowing water near 5th St. and Wilmot Rd. Flood waters also crossed roadways in Wilshire Heights near Broadway and Craycroft.

Thunderstorm winds several downed trees and power poles between Campbell Ave. and Palo Verde Rd. and between Drexel and Irvington Rds. About 2000 customers were without power and a section of Irvington Rd. was closed as a result. Tents at Community Food Bank were blown down causing closure of outdoor food distribution operations the following 2 days.
Thunderstorm winds snapped a power pole along State Rte. 82 near Fairbank.

More than one inch of rain in less than an hour caused a rapid rise in Alamo Wash where a storm had produced an inch of rain three hours earlier.  A motorist was rescued from a vehicle stuck in floodwaters on Chantilly Rd. at the Alamo Wash.

Two to four inches of rain in 3 hours in the southern Chiricahua Mountains caused flash flooding of streams over and west of the mountains. Two motorists in one vehicle were stuck in floodwaters east of McNeal on Davis Rd. near milepost 30. An elderly man attempted to drive through waters to rescue them when his vehicle was swept downstream. He was rescued but not before suffering hypothermia from being in the cold water.
A thunderstorm wind gust of 62 mph was reported at Safford Airport but no damage occurred.
Thunderstorm winds downed a power pole at Dawn and Houghton Rds. in Vail.

One to two inches of rain in less than an hour in Nogales, Sonora caused a rapid rise on Nogales Wash in Arizona, causing it to overtop its banks. Two drowning victims were washed across the border from Mexico and retrieved in Arizona.
More than 1 of rain in less than 1 hour in Vail caused flash flooding of roadways including Old Vail Rd. and Dawn Rd.
More than 1 inch of rain in less than an hour caused flash flooding in central and eastern Tucson. This includes roadways near the intersections of Speedway and Swan and Grant and 1st Ave.
Thunderstorm wind gusts downed two power poles near the school complex in Kearny, leaving nearly 1000 customers without power.
Thunderstorms winds downed two power poles in Catalina at Highway 77 near Graham Rd.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees along Dove Mountain Blvd. north of Moore Rd.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees near the intersection of Ina and Oracle Rds.
More than 1.5 of rain in 3 hours caused the Artesia Wash to flow swiftly and to flood Highway 86 west of Sells.

Very hot high temperatures of 104 to 115 degrees, or 8 to 12 degrees above normal, occurred in the lower deserts of Pima and Pinal counties August 3-4, and caused the High Heat Risk category to be reached. High temperatures on August 3 included 115 degrees at Ajo (record), 109 at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, 108 at Sells, and 104 at Picacho. On August 4 highs included 115 degrees at Ajo (tie), 110 at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, 109 at Sells (record), and 107 at Picacho. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one person found in the desert near San Miguel.

Very hot high temperatures of 101 to 107 degrees, or 8 to 12 degrees above normal, occurred in the lower elevations of Graham and eastern sections of Pinal and Pima counties on August 4, and caused the High Heat Risk category to be reached. High temperatures included 107 degrees at Tucson International Airport, 102 at Safford Airport, and 101 at Green Valley, San Manuel and Duncan. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one person found in the desert near Three Points.

Temperatures 5 degrees above normal, 95 to 100 degrees, occurred in the San Pedro River Valley of Cochise County causing the  Moderate Heat Risk category to be reached on  August 6. The Pima County Medical Examiner confirmed that heat was the primary cause of death for one male found near Palominas.

Very hot high temperatures of 104 to 114 degrees, or 5 to 11 degrees above normal, occurred in the lower elevations of Pima, southeast Pinal, and northwest sections of Cochise and Graham counties August 25-27 and caused the High Heat Risk category to be reached. The highest temperatures at select locations during the period were 114 degrees (tied record on 8/27) at Ajo, 112 (both records on 8/26 and 8/27) at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument, 111 (record on 8/26) at Sells, 108 (one degree shy of the record on 8/27) at Picacho, 106 on 8/26 at Tucson International Airport, 105 on 8/25 and 8/26 at San Carlos and 103 on 8/25 at Cascabel.

Thunderstorm winds caused considerable damage near the junction of Highways 70 and 191 in Safford. Two hotel marquis signs were blown down. A large roof extending to the side of a building near a skate park was damaged and an attached tall block wall also fell. A wall south of this property where an animal shelter was located blew down along with a power line that caused a funeral home's cold storage unit to lose power. Damage extended several blocks south to 15th St. where the roof was peeled off an apartment complex. allowing rain to enter one unit. A few other buildings in Safford sustained moderate roof damage and solid fencing partitions were blown down. Several trees were blown down, some of which caused additional roof damage. causing roof damage. Some other tree/power line damage in other parts of town. A recreational vehicle was  flipped on its side 5 miles south of Safford. The ASOS at Safford Municipal Airport measured a gust to 68 mph at 1545MST.
A wind gust to 66 mph was measured near Old Spanish Trail and Freeman Rd.
Nearly 1.5 of rain in about 30 minutes caused flash flooding of streets in Safford.

Lightning struck and damaged a block wall near Snyder and Sabino Canyon Rds.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees in Saddlebrooke One and blew numerous roof tiles off one residence.

High winds buffeted eastern Santa Cruz and southwest Cochise counties during the late night hours of October 11 and early morning hours of October 12. Sustained winds over 40 mph and wind gusts of 50 to 70 mph were measured at a number of observing sites for several hours. The highest gust recorded was 70 mph at the Libby Field ASOS at 0017MST. High winds downed or damaged 16 power poles in the Sierra Vista, Fort Huachuca and Hereford areas and other damage was reported to roofs, windows, fences, vehicles and trees. Downed power lines near Fort Huachuca sparked the Site Maverick wildfire that consumed over 1800 acres of grassland before firefighters achieved containment. Power lines were also downed in the Sonoita area.

High winds buffeted northeast Cochise county during the late night hours of October 11 and early morning hours of October 12. Sustained winds over 40 mph and wind gusts of 50 to 65 mph were measured at state DOT sites along Interstate 10 downwind of Dos Cabezas and the Chiricahua Mountains. The highest gust recorded was 65 mph at San Simon at 0243MST. High winds downed 2 power poles in the Elfrida area.

High winds buffeted southwest Cochise County during the early morning hours of December 15. Sustained winds over 40 mph and wind gusts of 50 to just shy of 70 mph were measured at a number of observing sites for several hours. The highest gust recorded was 68 mph on the southwest side of Sierra Vista at 0124MST.
